Who We Are

The Constructive Dialogue Institute (CDI) is a non-partisan, non-profit dedicated to equipping the next generation of Americans with the skills to communicate and collaborate across lines of difference. We work with U.S. colleges and universities by providing co-curricular programming for students, professional development for faculty and staff, and strategic guidance to leadership. Our goal is to foster constructive dialogue at every level of the institution and to create the conditions for lasting organizational change. CDI was co-founded by psychologist Jonathan Haidt, the bestselling author of The Righteous Mind and The Anxious Generation.

The Role

CDI is looking for an Associate Director or Director of Development to run our fundraising operations. You’ll report directly to our Co-Founder and Executive Director, who will continue to serve as CDI’s primary fundraiser. Your role will be to enable her fundraising in two key ways: (1) by running an exceptionally organized fundraising operation behind the scenes, and (2) by being responsible for grant writing and reporting responsibilities. This role combines meaningful ownership—you’ll operate with significant autonomy—with the chance to work with an experienced fundraiser and deepen your own expertise.

We’re looking for a development generalist with two super strengths: (1) operational excellence and (2) exceptional writing and communication skills. You bring rigor and organization to everything you touch, and you can make complex ideas clear and compelling without flattening their nuance. You notice details, anticipate what’s coming, and are always looking for a smarter way to run the work.

We’re open to candidates with different levels of fundraising experience. At the Director level, you’d take on more relationship management and strategy from the start; at the Associate Director level, you’d have room to grow into those responsibilities over time. What matters most to us is that you take real pride in the quality of your work and believe deeply in CDI’s mission.

What You’ll Do

Grant Writing & Management

  • Lead development and submission of compelling grant proposals, reports, and donor materials.

  • Translate CDI’s work and impact into clear, compelling narratives that resonate with funders while staying true to CDI’s voice and strategy.

  • Collaborate closely with Finance, Marketing & Communications, and program teams across CDI to gather the content needed for grant proposals and reports.

  • Maintain an exceptionally high bar for both the quality of all grant materials and the efficiency of the processes behind them.

  • Maintain a comprehensive grants calendar; proactively manage all deadlines for grants and other funder commitments.

Development Operations

  • Own the systems and infrastructure behind CDI’s fundraising work, from HubSpot and funder records to internal workflows and documentation.

  • Maintain and refine core assets, including reusable grant content, case studies, pitch decks, templates, and annual reports.

  • Partner closely with Finance to process new contributions, track grant requirements, and maintain funder and grant documentation.

  • Keep CDI’s fundraising pipeline current and actionable; partner with Finance to translate that pipeline into revenue projections.

  • Build and continuously improve the workflows, tools, and systems that keep CDI’s fundraising function running smoothly.

Fundraising Strategy & Relationships

  • Proactively manage the preparation and follow-through around the Executive Director’s funder relationships, enabling her to focus on relationship building.

  • Support the Executive Director in shaping fundraising strategy and priorities.

  • Conduct prospect and landscape research to identify new funding opportunities and inform fundraising strategy.

  • Depending on experience, directly manage and steward a portfolio of funder relationships.

Requirements

Who You Are

  • 5+ years of experience in development or fundraising, including experience writing successful grants in the six- and seven-figure range.

  • Passionate about development operations, with experience building systems and processes that keep fundraising work running exceptionally smoothly, particularly in smaller or growing organizations.

  • An excellent writer and communicator who can make complex ideas clear and compelling for different audiences.

  • Exceptionally organized and self-directed; you keep work moving, stay ahead of deadlines, and require minimal oversight.

  • Exceptionally detail-oriented, with a very high bar for quality and accuracy.

  • Strong judgment; you notice nuance, anticipate issues before they happen, and can assess what requires attention or escalation.

  • Passionate about constructive dialogue and aligned with CDI’s values.

For the Director role, we’ll also look for:

  • 7+ years of progressively responsible experience in development or fundraising, including 2+ years in management or leadership roles.

  • Experience owning funder relationships through cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.

  • Experience building and executing fundraising strategies to achieve philanthropic revenue goals of $1 million or more.

What We Offer

  • A Mission-Driven Culture — our work culture genuinely reflects our mission, characterized by intellectual humility, continuous improvement, and open-mindedness

  • Unlimited PTO — recharge on your own schedule with unlimited paid time off, in addition to 13 company holidays

  • Health, Vision & Dental — health, vision, and dental plans through, with CDI contributing toward your premiums each month

  • 401(k) Match — invest in your future with a 100% match on your contributions, up to 3% of your pay

  • Professional Development — an annual budget to invest in your growth: build new skills, deepen existing ones, and stay inspired in your work

  • Remote Work Support — up to $500 reimbursed for home office equipment and up to $50/month reimbursed for home internet or cell phone expenses

The Details

  • Compensation: Associate Director: $101,000–$113,000; Director: $132,000–$147,000

  • Reports to: Executive Director

  • Direct reports: None

  • Schedule: Full-time, flexible within U.S. time zones

  • Target start date: ASAP

  • Location: Remote, must be based in the U.S.


A note on AI: We know AI has become a useful writing assistant, and we’re comfortable with candidates using it that way. But when AI does too much of the writing, applications start to sound remarkably similar, making it hard for us to understand what you uniquely bring to the table. Please keep this in mind as you prepare your application.

Highlights

CDI is hiring a resourceful, detail-oriented Director of Development Operations to own our fundraising systems, relationships, and grant process, and support our Executive Director.

Location: Remote (U.S.)
Clearance: U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident Required with the ability to obtain a Public Trust
Salary Range: 120K – 135K

LTS is seeking an experienced ServiceNow System Administrator to support the implementation, configuration, security, governance, and ongoing administration of the ServiceNow platform supporting a mission-critical Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) program.

The ServiceNow System Administrator will play a key role in establishing foundational platform standards, administrative processes, environment controls, user and access governance, security configurations, integrations, and operational procedures. This individual will work closely with platform architects, developers, cybersecurity personnel, infrastructure teams, and program leadership to ensure the ServiceNow environment is secure, stable, supportable, compliant, and governed in alignment with VA OIT standards and federal cybersecurity requirements.

This is an opportunity to help establish and mature a ServiceNow environment within a complex federal enterprise while contributing directly to platform reliability, security, governance, and modernization.

What You’ll Do:

  • Support the initial configuration and operationalization of ServiceNow instances across development, test, staging, and production environments, including platform settings, plugins, properties, user/group structures, and administrative standards.
    • Manage, configure, and maintain ServiceNow instances to ensure platform availability, performance, stability, security, and supportability.
    • Prepare and support ServiceNow instance clones, upgrades, health checks, patching, release activities, and other advanced platform administration activities.
    • Establish and administer controlled promotion of configuration changes between environments using approved ServiceNow deployment mechanisms and change processes.
    • Manage activation and configuration of ServiceNow plugins and platform capabilities in accordance with architecture, security, licensing, and governance requirements.
    • Monitor instance health, platform performance, diagnostics, scheduled jobs, logs, integrations, and technical debt; identify and remediate platform health findings.
    • Provide day-to-day platform administration, end-user provisioning, and primary ITSM ticket triage for ServiceNow-related requests and issues.
    • Help establish and enforce ServiceNow platform governance, including configuration standards, naming conventions, administrative procedures, development controls, environment management, and release processes.
    • Review proposed platform changes for alignment with ServiceNow architecture, security, governance, and configuration standards.
    • Maintain platform configuration records, administrative SOPs, environment diagrams, access matrices, operational runbooks, and other governance documentation.
    • Support change management processes, including CAB and RFC activities, in alignment with VA governance requirements.
    • Ensure ServiceNow configurations and connected technologies adhere to applicable VA TRM-approved technologies and standards.
    • Configure and maintain ServiceNow users, groups, roles, ACLs, and role-based access controls using least-privilege and separation-of-duties principles.
    • Support ServiceNow security controls, including authentication/SSO integrations, MFA dependencies, encryption, audit logging, privileged access, and secure configuration standards.
    • Establish and maintain controls for service accounts, privileged accounts, API credentials, certificates, and secrets, including access reviews and credential rotation.
    • Configure and maintain auditing, transaction logging, access logging, and supporting evidence required for security assessments and Authority to Operate (ATO) activities.
    • Support compliance with applicable VA cybersecurity policies, FISMA, NIST 800-53, Zero Trust principles, and VAAR/FAR requirements.
    • Partner with ISSOs and cybersecurity personnel on vulnerability remediation, POA&M updates, continuous monitoring, audit readiness, STIGs, CIS benchmarks, and secure configuration baselines.
    • Support ServiceNow integration with enterprise identity services, including Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID.
    • Support and administer ServiceNow integrations using MID Servers, APIs, integration accounts, connection aliases, credentials, and endpoints.
    • Coordinate with VA cloud, network, database, identity, and infrastructure teams on dependencies affecting platform availability, security, disaster recovery, and continuity of operations.
    • Diagnose and resolve ServiceNow platform, integration, authentication, and application issues using system logs, transaction logs, scheduled job history, integration logs, and platform diagnostic capabilities.
    • Provide Tier 2/3 support for ServiceNow incidents, service requests, and escalations.
    • Collaborate with developers, architects, DevOps engineers, cybersecurity teams, network teams, and VA stakeholders to resolve cross-functional technical issues.
    • Participate in Agile ceremonies and contribute to iterative delivery cycles.
    • Recommend opportunities to improve platform performance, modernization, operational efficiency, security posture, and technical debt.

What We’re Looking For:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field or equivalent relevant professional experience.
    • 5+ years of system administration or platform administration experience within enterprise or federal environments.
    • 3+ years of hands-on ServiceNow platform administration experience.
    • Demonstrated experience configuring ServiceNow users, groups, roles, ACLs, authentication, instance properties, plugins, notifications, scheduled jobs, integrations, and platform security controls.
    • Experience supporting ServiceNow implementations or initial platform setup across development, test, staging, and production environments.
    • Hands-on experience with ServiceNow instance upgrades, clones, health checks, release management, and configuration promotion.
    • Experience establishing or operating within a ServiceNow platform governance model, including configuration standards, change controls, and administrative procedures.
    • Knowledge of ServiceNow security architecture, least-privilege access design, audit logging, privileged access, and secure integration practices.
    • Experience supporting SSO and identity integrations, preferably with Active Directory and/or Microsoft Entra ID.
    • Knowledge of federal cybersecurity frameworks, STIGs, secure configuration practices, and ATO support activities.
    • Experience documenting platform configurations, administrative procedures, security controls, and operational standards.
    • Strong ServiceNow troubleshooting experience using platform logs, scheduled jobs, integration logs, and diagnostic capabilities.
    • Experience supporting VA, DoD, HHS, or other federal agencies is strongly desired.
    • Excellent communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work effectively across technical, cybersecurity, program, and government stakeholder teams.

Nice to Have:

  • ServiceNow Certified System Administrator (CSA) certification.
    • Additional ServiceNow certifications such as Certified Application Developer (CAD) or relevant implementation certifications.
    • Experience supporting VA systems and environments, including IAM and TRM-approved technologies.
    • Security+, ITIL, Microsoft, Red Hat, AWS, Azure Administrator, or other relevant technical certifications.
    • Experience with automation tools such as PowerShell, Bash, or Ansible.
    • Experience supporting cloud operations and modernization initiatives.

What’s in it for you?

The opportunity to support high visibility federal missions in IT and healthcare
A culture that values innovation, growth, collaboration, and quality
Access to cutting-edge tools and technologies
Comprehensive benefits for you and your family
A career path that rewards ambition and performance

If you’re ready to push boundaries, sharpen your skills, and join a team that is passionate about building what’s next, we’d love to meet you. Apply today and let’s build a future together!

LTS shares salary ranges to promote transparency. Compensation ranges are provided for informational purposes, and final compensation may vary based on experience, skills, location, and role requirements.

LTS is committed to offering eligible employees comprehensive benefits that will provide them with options intended to meet their needs and the needs of their family.

Our Children's Trust is a non-profit public interest law firm that provides strategic, campaign-based legal services to youth from diverse backgrounds to secure their legal rights to a safe climate. Praxis Precision Medicines is a fully integrated, clinical-stage precision neuroscience company that applies genetic insights to the discovery and development of therapies for rare and more prevalent neurological disorders. This is a program leadership role, not simply a writing role. You will become deeply fluent in the program—its mechanism, evidence, development strategy, competitive landscape, and evolving data—and use that understanding to define how its scientific story should develop over time. You will connect ideas and evidence across functions so that regulatory submissions, clinical publications, and Medical Affairs and Commercial communications reinforce one scientifically rigorous and differentiated story.

Success requires curiosity to get deep into the science, judgment to determine what matters, and the influence to align people who may see the program through very different lenses. You will work closely with Regulatory Strategy, Clinical Development, Nonclinical, Medical Affairs, Commercial, and other partners, challenging assumptions when needed and creating clarity when the data or path forward is complex.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Own the strategic scientific narrative for a lead Praxis program, building deep fluency in its science, data, development strategy, competitive context, and potential value to patients and translating that knowledge into a clear, differentiated messaging framework.
  • Build and maintain a forward-looking narrative and communications roadmap that connects program strategy, emerging evidence, key milestones, regulatory interactions, publications, and launch preparation rather than treating each deliverable as a standalone event.
  • Shape the scientific positioning and key messages within critical clinical and regulatory documents, including protocols, investigator brochures, clinical study reports, briefing documents, clinical overviews, and integrated summaries; directly author or lead authoring of high-impact documents when needed.
  • Set narrative direction for US and global regulatory submissions, including INDs, NDAs, and MAAs, partnering closely with Regulatory Affairs, regulatory writing, Clinical Development, and program teams to ensure the evidence tells a clear, rigorous, and consistent story.

jobs.title: Director, Product Marketing
jobs.excerpt: About PAX PAX is a leading global cannabis brand redefining how people experience the plant through thoughtful design, innovative technology, and a commitment to quality.
jobs.description:
About PAX

PAX is a leading global cannabis brand redefining how people experience the plant through thoughtful design, innovative technology, and a commitment to quality. For nearly two decades, PAX has crafted products that make cannabis simpler, more enjoyable, and more accessible, earning the trust of millions of consumers around the world.

Recognized by The New York Times’ Wirecutter, TIME, Fast Company, GQ, Gear Patrol, and more, PAX has built a brand at the intersection of cannabis, design, technology, and culture. We’re driven by the belief that cannabis can make life better, and that innovation can unlock its benefits in ways that set a higher standard for the category. Beyond our products, PAX is committed to moving the industry forward through advocacy, responsible access, social impact, and sustainability.

The Opportunity

PAX is seeking a Director of Product Marketing to lead product and portfolio marketing across our global device business and U.S. cannabis consumables business. This person will help determine where PAX plays, whom we serve, and how our products win. They will translate consumer insight, market dynamics, and business priorities into clear portfolio strategies, differentiated product positioning, and commercially rigorous go-to-market plans.

The Director will be involved throughout the product lifecycle, from opportunity identification and product definition through commercialization, launch, and ongoing optimization. They will serve as a critical connector among Product, Marketing, Creative, Sales, E-commerce, Operations, Finance, and Insights, ensuring every product has a clear consumer proposition, role within the portfolio, and plan for commercial success. The ideal candidate is a strategic thinker and strong operator who can move easily between shaping a product roadmap, refining a positioning statement, developing a global launch plan, and evaluating in-market performance.

ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Shape the Portfolio

  • Lead product marketing across PAX’s device and consumables portfolios.
  • Define each product’s audience, consumer need, value proposition, and role within the broader portfolio.
  • Turn consumer insights, category trends, and business data into product roadmap recommendations and compelling business cases.
  • Help shape portfolio architecture, pricing, and lifecycle strategies across formats, markets, channels, and price points.
  • Translate technical information into simple, differentiated benefits that matter.

Bring Products to Market

  • Own go-to-market strategy for new products, line extensions, relaunches, and other major portfolio initiatives.
  • Define the audience, positioning, channel strategy, commercial requirements, and success metrics for each launch.
  • Create clear, insight-led briefs that align Product, Creative, Brand, E-commerce, Sales, Trade Marketing, Communications, Operations, and Finance.
  • Adapt launch plans across PAX’s distinct channels, including e-commerce, domestic and international wholesale, and licensed dispensaries.
  • Keep teams focused and accountable, surfacing risks and driving decisions early enough to protect timing and quality.
  • Equip sales teams and channel partners with compelling product stories, training, and tools that drive sell-in and sell-through.

Drive the Business Forward

  • Own the ongoing commercial health of products beyond launch, developing lifecycle strategies that sustain relevance, velocity, and profitability over time.
  • Build a deep understanding of how consumers discover, evaluate, purchase, and repurchase PAX products across channels.
  • Track product and launch performance across revenue, distribution, velocity, conversion, consumer response, and profitability.
  • Identify and lead lifecycle opportunities including pricing and promotion, bundles, product refreshes, new channel or market expansion, repositioning, and end-of-life planning.
  • Partner with Brand, E-commerce, Sales, and Trade Marketing to evolve messaging, content, merchandising, and demand-driving programs based on product performance and consumer behavior.
  • Turn performance data, competitive intelligence, and partner feedback into clear recommendations for how to accelerate, optimize, or rationalize the portfolio.
  • Lead post-launch and ongoing business reviews, translating insights into specific actions, owners, and success metrics.
  • Build repeatable processes that bring greater clarity, rigor, and accountability to how PAX launches, grows, and manages products throughout their lifecycle.

How You’ll Work

  • Bring structure and clarity to complex, fast-moving work.
  • Build trust across teams and lead effectively through influence.
  • Balance strong strategic thinking with a willingness to get into the details.
  • Communicate clearly, make thoughtful recommendations, and push decisions forward.
  • Stay curious about consumers, the category, and what the data is telling us.
  • Operate with high ownership, sound judgment, and low ego.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 8-12+ years of experience in product marketing, portfolio strategy, or commercialization.
  • Demonstrated success leading complex product launches across multiple channels, markets, or business models.
  • Strong experience in consumer insight, segmentation, positioning, messaging and consumer-facing product copy, pricing, and go-to-market strategy.
  • A proven ability to translate consumer needs and technical product details into differentiated, commercially effective stories.
  • Experience partnering closely with Product, Sales, Creative, Operations, and Finance teams.
  • Strong commercial and analytical judgment, including the ability to evaluate market opportunities and product performance.
  • Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to influence leaders and cross-functional teams.
  • Brings structure, clarity, and momentum to fast-paced work with evolving priorities.
  • Hands-on approach and willingness to operate at both strategic and executional levels.
  • Experience in consumer tech, CPG, wellness, cannabis, or another regulated category.
  • Experience with wholesale, retail, DTC, and/or dispensary channels.
  • Genuine enthusiasm about cannabis consumers and building the future of the category.

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Compensation

In addition to the benefits below, this role has a pay range between $160,000 and $210,000 and equity. The pay range represents what we believe, in good faith, this role will pay. The final salary offer will be determined based on a variety of factors including, but not limited to, depth of experience, geographic location, and relevant education or training.

We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, perform essential job functions, and receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

jobs.description:
Venha fazer parte de um ecossistema vivo onde o futuro dos negócios é criado e vivido todos os dias. Faça parte desta transformação!

Requisitos:
Atuar como referência técnica na definição da arquitetura corporativa de identidade digital, suportando decisões de autenticação, autorização, governança de identidades e integração entre plataformas.
Analisar, desenhar e implementar soluções de IAM e CIAM.
Desenhar fluxos de autenticação, autorização e gestão do ciclo de vida de identidades.
Desenvolver e evoluir APIs, microserviços e componentes de segurança.
Definir padrões técnicos e boas práticas de desenvolvimento seguro (SSDLC).
Realizar integrações síncronas e assíncronas com plataformas internas e externas via APIs, eventos e mensageria.
Participar de refinamentos técnicos, requisitos não funcionais e revisões de arquitetura.
Contribuir para a esteira DevSecOps e para a qualidade de software.
Apoiar a resolução de incidentes complexos e análises de causa raiz.
Atuar como referência em identidade digital, autenticação e segurança de aplicações.

Requisitos obrigatórios — Desenvolvimento e Arquitetura
Experiência como Analista de Sistemas, Desenvolvedor Sênior ou funções correlatas.

Domínio de C# e ecossistema .NET.

Desenvolvimento de APIs REST e microserviços.
Padrões de integração corporativa (Enterprise Integration Patterns).
Integrações síncronas e assíncronas; gRPC e Message Brokers.
Arquitetura orientada a eventos (Event-Driven) e Kafka (produção e consumo).
Ciclo completo de desenvolvimento (SDLC).
Clean Architecture, Hexagonal Architecture, DDD, CQRS, Mediator Pattern, Event Sourcing (desejável) e arquiteturas distribuídas.
Modelagem de dados / Entidade-Relacionamento; bancos Oracle e Redis.

Requisitos obrigatórios — Identidade Digital
Experiência comprovada em implementação, customização ou sustentação de ao menos uma plataforma IAM/CIAM corporativa (ex.: ForgeRock, Ping Identity, SailPoint, Saviynt, Keycloak, Microsoft Entra ID, Auth0 ou Okta).
Domínio avançado de protocolos e padrões: OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect (OIDC), SAML 2.0, JWT, SCIM, Federation e Single Sign-On (SSO).
Gestão de ciclo de vida de identidades; provisionamento e desprovisionamento; RBAC; ABAC; gestão de privilégios; Segregação de Funções (SoD); governança de acessos; MFA.

Requisitos obrigatórios — Segurança da Informação
Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SSDLC) e OWASP Top 10.
Criptografia simétrica e assimétrica, hash, password hash, assinatura digital e certificados digitais.
Conceitos de autenticação multifator (MFA).

Diferenciais desejáveis — Identidade Moderna
FIDO2, Passkeys, WebAuthn, Device Binding.
Adaptive Authentication e Risk-Based Authentication.

Diferenciais desejáveis — Governança (IGA)
Access Review e recertificação de acessos.
Joiner-Mover-Leaver, Birthright Access, Role Mining e Entitlement Management.
Identity Governance and Administration (IGA).

Diferenciais desejáveis — PAM
Privileged Access Management, gestão de contas privilegiadas e segregação de acessos administrativos.

Diferenciais desejáveis — Nuvem
IAM cloud-native em Azure, AWS ou GCP; Secrets Management, Managed Identities e federação entre ambientes.

Diferenciais desejáveis — Observabilidade
OpenTelemetry, Distributed Tracing, observabilidade aplicada a autenticação, SIEM e monitoramento de fraudes de autenticação.

Diferenciais desejáveis — Contexto regulatório
Experiência em ambientes regulados: instituições financeiras, cooperativas de crédito, seguradoras, fintechs ou meios de pagamento.

Soft Skills - Descreva detalhadamente as habilidades interpessoais necessárias:Capacidade analítica e resolução de problemas complexos: aptidão para compreender cenários de integração complexos, identificar causas raiz e propor soluções escaláveis e seguras.

Visão sistêmica e pensamento arquitetural: capacidade de entender impactos entre múltiplos sistemas, aplicações, processos de negócio e requisitos de segurança.

Comunicação eficaz: habilidade para traduzir conceitos técnicos para públicos não técnicos e atuar como ponte entre equipes de tecnologia, segurança, arquitetura, fornecedores e áreas de negócio.

Autonomia e senso de propriedade (ownership): capacidade de conduzir iniciativas de ponta a ponta, assumindo responsabilidade pelos resultados e atuando com baixa necessidade de supervisão.

Colaboração e trabalho em equipe: facilidade para atuar em ambientes multidisciplinares, colaborando com times de desenvolvimento, arquitetura, infraestrutura, segurança e produtos digitais.

Orientação a resultados: foco na entrega de valor para o negócio, priorizando atividades críticas e mantendo o equilíbrio entre agilidade, qualidade e segurança.

Adaptabilidade e aprendizado contínuo: disposição para acompanhar a rápida evolução das tecnologias de identidade, autenticação, APIs, nuvem e segurança.

Capacidade de influência e negociação: habilidade para conduzir discussões técnicas, alinhar interesses entre diferentes áreas e promover a adoção de boas práticas de identidade e acesso.

Mentalidade de segurança (Security by Design): preocupação constante em incorporar requisitos de segurança desde a concepção das integrações e soluções.

jobs.description:
Position Description

Valiant Solutions is seeking a Senior Systems Architect to join our rapidly growing and innovative cybersecurity team!

The Senior Systems Architect owns the operational, technical, and informational architecture for the client's cybersecurity systems within the Cybersecurity Services Division. The architect translates the client's strategic business and technical requirements into secure, scalable, cloud-native solutions and drives architectural activities aligned with the client's enterprise standards, Zero Trust principles, and Executive Order 14028. The role produces the Engineering Design Documents, blueprints, and control mappings that govern how cybersecurity capabilities including SIEM, SOAR, CDM, TDSP, EDR, AWS GovCloud services, and identity platforms integrate across the client environment.

Named one of the Best Places to Work in the Washington DC area for 12 consecutive years, Valiant is proud of our employee-centric culture and commitment to excellence. If you are interested in learning more about Valiant and this opportunity, we invite you to apply now!

Location: The Senior Systems Architect can expect 100% telework. Remote work requires a high level of trust in our employees, and we strictly adhere to the details outlined in our Remote Work Policy below.

Eligibility Requirements: U.S. Citizenship is required due to federal contract obligations, and applicants must be able to successfully pass a federal background investigation.

Required Experience:

  • Twelve or more years of experience supporting cybersecurity information technology.
  • Three or more years of experience supporting cloud-based solutions.
  • AWS Solution Architect certification (required).
  • Experience with the planning, management, leadership, and coordination of multiple concurrent tasks, each with strict deadlines, for a large-scale cybersecurity design integrated with business-critical systems.
  • Demonstrated understanding of the software development, enhancement, and maintenance lifecycle.
  • Ability to perform complex technical tasks.
  • Strong technical understanding of cybersecurity deployment, functionality, and operation of capabilities including SIEM, EDR, CDM, penetration testing, DevSecOps, Identity and Access Management, and AWS GovCloud systems.
  • Experience with EKS, ECS, and containerized environments.
  • Strong knowledge of recent technological advances in computer science and engineering.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Required to obtain and maintain a Non-Sensitive / High Risk (Public Trust) security clearance, Tier 4/6c.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Additional AWS certifications such as AWS Certified Security – Specialty, AWS Certified DevOps Engineer, or AWS Certified Advanced Networking – Specialty.
  • Working knowledge of NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 (Systems Security Engineering), NIST SP 800-207 (Zero Trust Architecture), OMB M-22-09, and Executive Order 14028.
  • Experience with FedRAMP-approved cloud service provider integration in federal environments.
  • Familiarity with Infrastructure-as-Code tools (Terraform, CloudFormation) and policy-as-code frameworks.
  • Familiarity with the client Technology Standards and Products Guide and client Lifecycle Management Methodology (LMM).

Responsibilities:

  • Own the operational, technical, and informational architectures supporting client's cybersecurity systems and services.
  • Discern customer requirements, validate that architecture models address them, and confirm technical requirements and architecture quality attributes before designs move forward.
  • Develop and explain IT solutions grounded in client's strategic business and technical requirements, defining the structuring approach for each application and the appropriate use of technology.
  • Design and validate enterprise security architectures aligned with Zero Trust principles and NIST SP 800-207, including identity-centric access control, micro-segmentation, continuous monitoring, and least-privilege enforcement.
  • Lead development of Engineering Design Documents (EDDs), architecture blueprints, control implementation matrices, current and target state diagrams, data flow diagrams, and security zone definitions.
  • Design, integrate, and govern enterprise cloud architecture solutions on AWS GovCloud, with focus on EKS, ECS, and containerized environments.
  • Design and maintain security controls that support CI/CD and DevOps infrastructure, integrating with client's DevSecOps pipelines.
  • Direct the integration of SIEM, SOAR, CDM, TDSP, EDR, AWS cloud-native services, and identity platforms across the client cybersecurity tool portfolio.
  • Manage IT applications projects, including the design, development, and implementation of components of the IT architecture, and oversee solution roadmaps from vision through execution.
  • Develop and communicate architectural proposals for projects and initiatives, including comparative analyses, implementation roadmaps, cost, risk, and operational impact.
  • Develop and coordinate IT strategy and oversee implementation of integrated systems, replacing legacy solutions with modern alternatives per the lifecycle management strategy.
  • Collaborate with business owners, analysts, engineers, development teams, and infrastructure services to define, establish, and communicate application and data architecture standards, policies, and directions.
  • Design, validate, and implement scalable system infrastructure, and evaluate complex systems architecture for performance and efficiency improvements.
  • Maintain and evaluate current equipment and recommend modernization, cloud migration, and secure system design approaches.
  • Manage cloud design efforts, ensuring designs address organizational goals, security requirements, and FedRAMP-approved cloud package use.
  • Participate in architecture governance boards, technical working groups, the Engineering Review Board, and the Change Control Board, providing briefings and technical input to senior leadership.

About Valiant Solutions

Valiant Solutions is a security-focused IT solutions provider with public clients nationwide. Named one of the fastest growing privately held companies by Inc. 5000, Washington Technology’s Fast 50, and Washington Business Journal’s Best Places to Work in the D.C. area, Valiant Solutions prides itself on providing its employees with great benefits and career development opportunities. As a company, we are just as committed to growing careers as we are to building world-class IT solutions, all while enjoying an unparalleled work-life balance. We are in a phase of tremendous growth and building the team that will take us to the next level. We seek people whose talents and accomplishments will contribute to a thriving company, who have the character to support their capacity, and can make a positive impact on our culture. Alongside our talented team, you’ll learn to think quickly on your feet and expand your own personal and professional skill set. Our management team will inspire you to consider new perspectives and challenge you to become a better practitioner in the fast-paced industry of IT security. We hire people we respect – and we trust them to deliver results leveraging their expertise. If you would enjoy working in a dynamic environment as part of a stellar team of professionals, then we invite you to apply online today.

Remote Work Policy

Remote work necessitates a high level of trust in our employees. To ensure that employee performance does not suffer in a remote work environment, all employees who telecommute are expected to have a quiet and distraction-free workspace with adequate internet, dedicate their full attention and availability to their job duties during working hours, and maintain a schedule during core business hours that align with those of their coworkers and Valiant's clients. In alignment with Valiant's inclusive and engaging environment, cameras are encouraged and can be required to be on during virtual video conferences. Additionally, in alignment with the Office of the Inspector General’s effort to eliminate conflicting employment, all Valiant employees are required to disclose any current or future outside employment engagements. During onboarding and throughout employment, employees must disclose any current activities or intent to engage in outside employment or other professional activities and obtain written approval. Employees may not solicit or conduct any outside business during core business hours for Valiant Solutions and our clients.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Valiant Solutions is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, or veteran status, in accordance with applicable law.

Physical Demands

Sitting or standing at a desk for prolonged periods of time and consistent operation of a computer. Frequent communication and exchanging of accurate information via electronic communication, phones, and in person. Occasionally lift and/or move moderate amounts of weight, typically less than 20 pounds. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job.

Authorization to Share Resume and Personal Information

By submitting your resume for this position, you authorize Valiant Solutions to share your resume, as well as, personal information included on the resume, with its subsidiaries, affiliates and teaming partners for the purpose of considering you for this position and other available positions requiring comparable skills, education and experience. Details:

Ontario's Public Safety Radio Network (PSRN) is one of the largest and most complex public safety radio networks in North America. It covers approximately 750,000 km2 of area. PSRN serves more than 38,000 front-line and emergency responders, such as, police officers, fire service staff, ambulance paramedics, with the radio communications technology, equipment, and other resources that they need to keep Ontarians safe. Responders use this technology to communicate with their dispatchers and one another when responding to emergencies.

Emergency Services Telecommunications Division (ESTD) under the Ministry of Solicitor General (SOLGEN), has undertaken an ambitious project to upgrade the PSRN system. The network will be made more modern and compatible with other networks in the country. A supplier has been selected to provide equipment and services. ESTD is executing this large project in collaboration with other ministries and partners, such as, ministry of health, ministry of Natural Resources and Forestry, Ontario Provincial Police etc.

The project is governed by an empowered steering committee comprising leaders from all the stakeholder entities.

While detailed planning for the implementation is underway, some work of different project workstreams' is also being executed. Key activities of the project fall under the category of, business analysis, vendor coordination, stakeholder management, training, organization change management, project governance, radio resources acquisition and deployment, network design and design changes, radio site readiness (civil work included), planning and execution of transition from old to new network, service management etc.

  • Extensive experience in systems analysis and design in large systems environments

  • Experience developing, recommending, implementing and managing technical architecture
  • Experience in the use of Computer Aided Software Engineering (CASE) tools and other software tools such as project management tools
  • Awareness of emerging technologies, trends and directions
  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills; verbal and written communication skills; interpersonal and negotiation skills A team player with a track record for meeting deadlines
  • Experience in developing enterprise architecture deliverables (e.g. models)

jobs.description:
Who is American College of Education

Founded in 2005, American College of Education continues to be a leader in professional development through our online programs. The mission of ACE is to deliver high-quality, affordable, and accessible online programs grounded in evidence-based content, real-world experience and relevant application that places our students’ needs first.

ACE is a mission-driven institution continually recognized for its commitment to social responsibility and positive impact. As an Impact Institution, we believe we have a responsibility to our students, alumni, employees, communities, and society as a whole. Guided by our core values, we strive to create meaningful impact that extends well beyond our bottom line.

We prioritize candidate safety. Please note that all official communication will only come from our verified company email domain @Rippling.com

Who You Are
You are passionate about helping students achieve their educational goals. You thrive in a competitive and collaborative team environment. You are comfortable working remotely and have experience collaborating with others in a virtual environment. You possess a strong attention to detail.

As an Adjunct Faculty for American College of Education, you maintain a strong academic presence and growth in professional development for teaching, scholarly or creative works, and service to the profession and to the college. You report and work directly under the leadership of the department chair who provides guidance regarding 1) academic and teaching responsibilities, 2) service to students, department, college, and community, and 3) professional development.

Compensation

ACE is committed to paying a competitive wage while staying true to our mission of maintaining high-quality, affordable programs for our students. Adjuncts are paid per student per course here at ACE, and in general, the pay is $50/student at the bachelor and master levels and $126/student at the doctorate level. There are also opportunities to serve on paid committees, as well as receive payment for writing and developing courses.

What We Look for in the Ideal Candidate

  • Demonstrates self-reliance by meeting/exceeding workflow needs.
  • Demonstrates positive attitude and motivation, concern for students, teamwork, and excellent time management skills.
  • Follows established processes as outlined by the organization and leadership.
  • Completes assigned duties based on daily business needs and individual skill set.
  • Consistently produces a high volume of quality work.
  • Capable, and adapts as needed, to work under pressure and meet tight deadlines.
  • Proven ability to work independently with limited supervision and with other department personnel.
  • Must support and embrace the embrace the College's Impact mission to improve the people and communities we serve through our civic engagement initiatives.
  • Must have exceptional communication, organization, and time management skills.
  • Must be "self-motivated" as well as creative and efficient in proposing solutions to complex, time-critical problems.
  • Must be collaborative in driving decisions and a team player.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a high attention to detail.
  • Builds and maintains student satisfaction.
  • Recognizes and anticipates student needs.

Day to Day Responsibilities
In this role, you will wear different hats, but your skills will be especially essential in the following areas:

Academic and Teaching Responsibilities:

An adjunct faculty relates directly to students, handling instructional responsibilities to support, strengthen, and enhance the learning experience.

  • Interacts directly with students in an appropriate, professional manner.
  • Facilitates a safe and productive learning environment for students.
  • Responds in a timely manner to student requests for information, clarification of content, posts, and personal queries, and contacts inactive students as the need arises.
  • Oversees the quality of the course by reviewing the functionality and content, ensuring high-quality delivery of content.
  • Expands the student experience by “fingerprinting” the course content with unique personal experience, insights, or other professional knowledge.
  • Monitors and provides appropriate student feedback on assignments within college policies.
  • Synthesize and reports student performance data in a timeline manner.

Service to Students, Department, College and Community:

Faculty understand and support professional relationships within the course room, department, institution and beyond.

  • Supports the policies procedures and guidelines of the program and institution.
  • Aid student learning of ethical conduct, particularly related to plagiarism and copyright infringement; follows appropriate procedures in reporting infractions.
  • Directs students to supplemental resources as needed to enhance their individual skills and abilities.
  • Works collaboratively with colleagues and leadership of the college including attending required meetings.
  • Promotes the vision, mission, and culture of the college within and beyond the institution.
  • Provides appropriate leadership within one’s individual sphere of influence.

Professional Development:

As a demonstration of lifelong learning, faculty pursue endeavors to augment personal and professional skills.

  • Maintains a professional and technical knowledge of the curricula and industry by participating in leading-edge educational workshops/seminars, reviewing professional publications, establishing personal networks, and participating in professional societies. This includes maintaining a deep knowledge of emerging issues and trends related to the department.
  • Ensures the quality of program and course offerings by supporting and promoting research.

Qualifications and Education Requirements

  • Earned terminal degree(s) in a field associated with the department.
  • Minimum 5+ years in a leadership role leading others.
  • Must have a minimum of 3 peer-reviewed professional publications and presentations.
  • 1+ year(s) experience in teaching and leadership in a formal educational setting using both traditional and non-traditional teaching formats, higher education strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience in successfully developing online/virtual professional relationships.
  • Evidence of professional research and/or creative endeavors and expertise in the field.

Our Commitment to Employees

Just as we strive to empower our students for success, we also aim to enrich the lives of our employees. For 6 consecutive years, ACE was recognized as one of Indiana’s Best Places to Work, winning the #1 spot for medium-sized companies in 2020. In addition, ACE has earned national recognition, being named a USA Top Workplace in 2022, 2023 and 2024. As a virtual first organization, we celebrate diversity and are committed to creating a family-like inclusive work environment.

Physical Demands
The physical demand described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to communicate with and receive communications from students and ACE employees in real-time using online and other electronic media.

Commitment to Culture

At American College of Education, we’re all about building a one-of-a-kind, supportive community where everyone—students, faculty, and staff—can thrive. Guided by our mission and values, we focus on everything from innovative curriculum design to personalized instruction and student support to intentional planning, inclusive initiatives, and strategic resource allocation. We’re dedicated to creating an environment that celebrates freedom of expression, diversity of thought, open dialogue, and mutual respect. We believe in fostering a sense of belonging and wellness so that every member of our ACE family feels empowered, valued, and ready to reach their full potential. Together, we’re creating a vibrant, resilient, and connected learning community where everyone matters.

Additional Notes

This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Employees are increasingly integrating AI into their roles, demonstrating its potential to boost efficiency, accuracy, and productivity. By utilizing AI technologies, we can streamline processes, gain valuable insights from data, and automate routine tasks, which allows employees to concentrate on more strategic and creative aspects of their work. While AI is a beneficial tool in the workplace, if its use—such as ChatGPT, Grammarly, Copy.ai, etc.—accounts for more than 50% of any work assignments or job responsibilities, it will need to be reported to a direct leader.

Internet bandwidth speeds from an employee's remote work location must be a minimum of 50Mbps download speeds and 5Mbps upload speeds. Please note if the bandwidth is shared across multiple devices (tablets, computer, streaming, phone, etc.) you will need higher overall speeds. You can test the speed of your connection by visiting speedtest.net . Purchase, setup, installation, support, and ongoing maintenance of reliable internet service is the responsibility of the individual.

American College of Education seeks to attract and retain a diverse staff consistent with its diverse student body and surrounding communities. At this time we cannot consider candidates residing in Alaska, Washington D.C., Massachusetts, South Dakota, or Alabama.

ACE is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

ABOUT GREYSTAR


Greystar is a leading, fully integrated global real estate platform offering expertise in property management, investment management, development, and construction services in institutional-quality rental housing. Headquartered in Charleston, South Carolina, Greystar manages and operates over $350 billion of real estate in more than 260 markets globally with offices throughout North America, Europe, South America, and the Asia-Pacific region. Greystar is the largest operator of apartments in the United States, managing over one million units/beds globally. Across its platforms, Greystar has nearly $79 billion of assets under management, including over $34 billion of development assets and over $36.5 billion of regulatory assets under management. Greystar was founded by Bob Faith in 1993 to become a provider of world-class service in the rental residential real estate business. To learn more, visit .

JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY

Greystar is seeking an experienced, highly technical, hands-on, and mission-driven Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead engineering initiatives within our Digital, Data & AI team. The TPM will have a strong sense of ownership, aid in identifying and resolving dependencies, track progress across different teams, and ensure the work progresses, while clearly communicating progress and risks to project stakeholders.

This role sits at the delivery core of the Data Digital and AI team and is distinct from our Product Managers/Owners: PMs own the what and why (product direction and roadmap priorities); the TPM owns the how and when, driving execution end-to-end across engineering teams without absorbing product scope.

Success in this role requires an equal blend of hands-on technical fluency and strong project and program management discipline. Nearly every initiative brings together multiple engineering disciplines within a single project — data engineering, application/product engineering (web and mobile), and infrastructure.

JOB DESCRIPTION

JOB DESCRIPTION

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own end-to-end delivery for assigned initiatives, from scoping through launch, driving progress across data engineering, product engineering (web and mobile), and infrastructure teams, often within the same project.
  • Partner with Product Managers to translate product strategy and roadmaps into executable delivery plans. Product Managers own product direction; TPMs own sequencing, dependencies, and delivery risk.
  • Drive delivery for application-centric initiatives, including web and mobile feature launches, API/service integrations, and release coordination — with enough fluency in app architecture to pressure-test estimates, identify technical debt risk, and sequence frontend/backend/mobile workstreams realistically.
  • Keep initiatives moving under competing priorities by driving stalled decisions to resolution with clear options, a recommended default, and a named owner, rather than allowing work to drift.
  • Regularly assess risks and opportunities; understand best practices, drive process improvements, and find new ways of operating, with a focus on simplification and productivity.
  • Run the delivery operating system in Linear, including sprint planning, dependency tracking, RACI, and status reporting, as the single source of truth across multiple product teams.
  • Drive initiatives with a heavy data component, coordinating data readiness, integration, and quality across delivery, with enough fluency to pressure-test estimates and ensure data-dependent plans are realistic.

BASIC KNOWLEDGE & QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Proven track record of managing large-scale, complex technical initiatives for product development & software engineering with clear evidence of technical delivery you personally owned and shaped.
  • Demonstrated ability to work through ambiguity to detailed solutions. You can take a vague problem, crisply frame the challenge, identify a path forward, and drive an initiative over the finish line.
  • Self-motivated, proactive, and proven ability to adapt well and work with teams having different operating cadences.
  • Strong working knowledge of data, including the ability to read a data model, understand pipeline and integration dependencies, assess data quality, and hold teams accountable for data readiness. This is not a data engineering role, but you must be able to identify and address data-related risks.
  • Strong working knowledge of application development, including the ability to read a system/architecture diagram, understand client-server and API dependencies, assess technical debt and scalability tradeoffs, and hold teams accountable for release readiness. This is not a software engineering role, but you must be able to identify and address app-delivery risks
  • Experience developing processes where little exists and demonstrated flexibility to get things done.
  • Proven experience leading delivery across multiple engineering disciplines, not just one. You have coordinated data engineering, product or application engineering (web and/or mobile), and infrastructure within the same initiative.
  • Detail-oriented and able to understand the bigger picture by using your technical expertise and problem-solving abilities to prioritize and manage blocking issues.
  • Experience working in a highly cross-functional environment where communication with multiple groups is imperative.
  • Ability to build working knowledge quickly across unfamiliar technical areas. You will move between data, application, and infrastructure work and must understand each well enough to lead delivery and challenge engineering estimates.
  • Ability to ramp up quickly and learn new technologies with minimal lag time.
  • Excellent written and oral business communication and people skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders.
  • Experience with the Linear project management system or similar (Jira, Asana, etc).

The salary range for this position is $115,000 - $140,000 USD Annually.


Additional Compensation:


Many factors go into determining employee pay within the posted range including business requirements, prior experience, current skills and geographical location.

  • Corporate Positions: In addition to the base salary, this role may be eligible to participate in a quarterly or annual bonus program based on individual and company performance.
  • Onsite Property Positions: In addition to the base salary, this role may be eligible to participate in weekly, monthly, and/or quarterly bonus programs.

Robust Benefits Offered*:

  • Competitive Medical, Dental, Vision, and Disability & Life insurance benefits. Low (free basic) employee Medical costs for employee-only coverage; costs discounted after 3 and 5 years of service.
  • Generous Paid Time off. All new hires start with 15 days of vacation, 4 personal days, 10 sick days, and 11 paid holidays. Plus your birthday off after 1 year of service! Additional vacation accrued with tenure.
  • For onsite team members, onsite housing discount at Greystar-managed communities are available subject to discount and unit availability.
  • 6-Week Paid Sabbatical after 10 years of service (and every 5 years thereafter).
  • 401(k) with Company Match up to 6% of pay after 6 months of service.
  • Paid Parental Leave and lifetime Fertility Benefit reimbursement up to $10,000 (includes adoption or surrogacy).
  • Employee Assistance Program.
  • Critical Illness, Accident, Hospital Indemnity, Pet Insurance and Legal Plans.
  • Charitable giving program and benefits.

*Benefits offered for full-time employees. For Union and Prevailing Wage roles, compensation and benefits may vary from the listed information above due to Collective Bargaining Agreements and/or local governing authority.


Greystar will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.


Greystar is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.


This position may be performed remotely anywhere within the United States except the state of Alaska.


Important Notice: Greystar will never request your banking details or other sensitive personal information during the interview process. Greystar does not conduct any interviews via text or messaging, and all communication will come from official Greystar email addresses (@greystar.com). If you receive suspicious requests, please report them immediately to .

November 30, 2026

You built your career caring for women at a time when the healthcare system largely ignored them. You know HRT, you understand the complexity of perimenopause, and you’ve spent years earning the clinical instincts it takes to actually get this right. Now you want to do it at scale — for more patients, with fewer barriers, and in a practice model that matches how you already think and work.

That’s what Midi is. A fully virtual, fast-paced clinical environment built specifically around women’s midlife health — and designed for NPs who are ready to practice at their best.

THE ROLE

You’ll carry a full patient panel, managing perimenopause, menopause, weight, sexual health, mood, and sleep — all virtually. This is ongoing, relationship-based care, which means your patients come back to you — visit after visit, over months and years. You’ll prescribe and independently manage HRT (estrogen, progesterone, testosterone), evaluate patients for pharmacologic weight management including GLP-1 therapies, and make autonomous clinical decisions every day.

It’s a high-volume environment. Documentation, follow-through, and productivity benchmarks are part of the job — and the NPs who thrive here don’t fight that reality, they’re built for it. If you’re the kind of clinician who runs efficient visits without sacrificing warmth, closes every loop without being reminded, and moves comfortably between patients and platforms, you’ll feel at home here.

WHO THRIVES HERE

Our most successful NPs tend to share a few things in common:

  • They are genuinely passionate about women’s midlife health — this isn’t a stopover, it’s their calling
  • They are fluent with technology — EHR, video, AI scribe tools, Slack, clinical decision support — and they adapt quickly when tools change
  • They hold themselves to a high standard without needing to be managed toward it
  • They can carry a full panel, hit productivity targets, and still make every patient feel like the only one
  • They’ve practiced independently long enough to trust their own clinical judgment

Job Summary and Responsibilities

The System Senior Vice President (SVP), Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) oversees several areas of finance for CommonSpirit Health (CSH). The SVP leads a team responsible for all Financial Planning and activities for CSH. In addition, the SVP will lead teams overseeing all finance-related activities supporting Central and Corporate office functions, Operational Performance, Decision Support, and Value Capture. This leader plays a vital role in guiding the organization's financial decisions, supporting strategic initiatives and decision-making, and ensuring effective resource allocation to drive alignment and achieve CSH's short- and long-term operational and financial strategies and objectives. The SVP will serve as a thought partner to the CFO, COO, and CSO and work closely with other senior leaders across the organization to provide leadership and financial advice informing major strategic financial decisions and ensure organizational effectiveness and success. As the head of FP&A, this position provides the vision, strategic direction, and oversight for short- and long-range financial planning activities, capital allocations and approvals, growth initiatives, and strategic planning, including key initiative development and synergy realization, acquisitions and divestitures, and financial performance analysis, analytics, and management reporting. In addition, this leader is responsible for leading all finance activities related to the Corporate Office and Central Functions, including financial planning, capital allocation, performance and cost management, and analysis to support operational efficiency and growth.

  • Executive Leadership: Act as a strategic partner to the CFO and executive leadership team, providing financial insights and recommendations to drive business decisions. Collaborate with the CFO, COO, CSO, and other leaders to drive the system-wide strategic financial planning process, providing executive leaders and governance groups with views on financial implications and perspectives on business strategy, operations, and growth. Communicate financial strategies and results to C-suite, senior management, the Board of Directors, and other stakeholders.
  • Strategic Financial Planning: Develop, optimize, and lead the execution of the company's financial planning processes for capital expenses, operating expenses, and cash, including long-range planning, annual budgeting, and monthly and quarterly forecasting activities. Develop financial models and business case tools to support new business initiatives and investment decisions. Develop new integrated planning frameworks that provide better insights into prioritization, optimization, and utilization of assets and resources across the enterprise. Lead strategic financial planning discussions with the CFO, COO, CSO, and other senior executives and governance bodies on prioritizing and balancing operational performance, cash requirements, and capital spending levels. Provide financial insights and recommendations to support CSH's strategic short- and long-term plans and initiatives, ensuring alignment with expected funding levels, days cash on hand, debt-to-cap, and other key metrics. In collaboration with SVP Operational Finance, develop short- and long-range financial targets for CSH Consolidated and Regions.
  • Capital Deployment and Governance: Engage with COO, CFO, and CSO on matters related to system-wide capital capacity and recommend optimal allocations and investments. Further develop standards and processes for capital planning, prioritization, allocation, and deployment across the enterprise, including end-to-end business case creation, prioritization frameworks, and value-realization tracking. Create and maintain necessary updates to the CommonSpirit Capital Policy and Procedures.
  • Financial Analysis and Performance Monitoring: In collaboration with other finance functions, develop and optimize frameworks and systems for financial analysis, management reporting, and performance monitoring, including preparation of detailed financial analyses, scenario planning, sensitivity analysis, variance analysis, expected return on projects and capital, and other ad hoc analysis. Utilize advanced financial systems and tools to improve data accuracy and reporting capabilities. Establish key performance indicators (KPIs) and benchmarks to monitor financial performance when appropriate. Provide insights to executive leadership and governance groups related to quality of earnings, financial forecasts, capital, projected cash balances, key business metrics, and potential risks to achieve goals.
  • Business Partnering: Collaborate with business unit leaders, including Regional CFOs and other finance leaders, to understand their financial needs and provide support for budgeting, forecasting, and performance management. Support M&A activities by providing financial analysis and due diligence on the overall impact of potential acquisitions, partnerships, and divestitures, and by integrating acquired entities into the company's financial planning processes and systems.
  • Risk Management: Monitor and manage financial risks, including operational, market, regional, and strategic risks. Develop integrated scenario planning and work with Regional CFOs, Operational Finance, Treasury, and other leaders to develop views and provide perspective into long-term external market dynamics, industry trends, potential changes and implications to each region, the impact that different factors could have on overall organizational performance, and proposed actions the organization could take. Develop risk mitigation strategies and ensure compliance with financial policies and regulatory requirements.

Job Requirements

Required

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field; MBA or relevant advanced degree and 10+ years minimum of 10 years of healthcare Finance experience.

Preferred

  • Master's Degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field; MBA or relevant advanced degree and 10+ years minimum of 10 years of healthcare Finance experience.

Where You’ll Work

Inspired by faith. Driven by innovation. Powered by humankindness. CommonSpirit Health is building a healthier future for all through its integrated health services. As one of the nation’s largest nonprofit Catholic healthcare organizations, CommonSpirit Health delivers more than 20 million patient encounters annually through more than 2,300 clinics, care sites and 137 hospital-based locations, in addition to its home-based services and virtual care offerings. CommonSpirit has more than 157,000 employees, 45,000 nurses and 25,000 physicians and advanced practice providers across 24 states and contributes more than $4.2 billion annually in charity care, community benefits and unreimbursed government programs. Together with our patients, physicians, partners, and communities, we are creating a more just, equitable, and innovative healthcare delivery system.

HBX Group is the world’s leading technology partner, connecting and empowering the world of travel. We’re game-changers, disruptors, the people who bring together local and global brands in accommodation, transport, activities and payments through our network of 300,000 hotels worldwide, 60,000 hard to reach high value clients such as tour operators, travel agents and loyalty schemes across 140 source markets. We are tech-driven, with a customer-first philosophy, and commercial teams whose knowledge and relationships on the ground are second to none. And of course we have an amazing team! Our people, Team HBX Group, are the beating heart of the company who we encourage to ‘move fast, dream big and make the difference’ every day. In fact, we believe that it is tech + data + people that truly sets us apart in the market, alongside our ‘global approach, local touch’ mentality. We’re headquartered in Palma, Mallorca and employ around 3,500 people worldwide.


JOB DESCRIPTION:

About Us

HBX Group is the world’s leading technological partner, connecting and empowering the world of travel. We bring together global and local brands in accommodation, transport, activities and payments, serving 300,000 hotels and 60,000 hard‑to‑reach, high‑value clients across 140 source markets. Tech-driven with a customer-first mindset, our commercial teams and talented HBX people are the heart of what makes us unique. At HBX, we believe that tech + data + people set us apart, supported by our “global approach, local touch” philosophy.


Job Summary

We are seeking a commercially driven Key Account Manager to manage and grow a portfolio of travel agency partners, driving revenue, profitability, and client retention across a designated region. The role focuses on developing strategic client relationships, identifying new business opportunities, negotiating commercial agreements, and delivering sustainable sales growth through data-driven account management.


Key Responsibilities

  • Manage and grow a portfolio of travel agency accounts to achieve revenue and profitability targets.
  • Analyse account performance to identify growth opportunities and reduce churn.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with key travel trade partners.
  • Negotiate and manage commercial agreements.
  • Drive new business acquisition and account development initiatives.
  • Act as the primary point of contact for assigned clients.
  • Collaborate with internal teams to align commercial strategies and deliver client objectives.
  • Conduct client meetings, business reviews, and on-site sales visits.
  • Represent the company at industry events, conferences, and trade shows.
  • Identify client needs and recommend solutions to maximize business growth and product distribution.

Required Skills & Experience

  • 3-5 years of sales or account management experience within the travel industry, preferably retail travel.
  • Proven track record of managing client portfolios and delivering against sales targets and budgets.
  • Strong commercial acumen with experience driving revenue growth and profitability.
  • Excellent relationship-building, communication, negotiation, and influencing skills.
  • Analytical mindset with the ability to interpret performance data and identify growth opportunities.
  • Strong presentation, stakeholder management, and customer-facing skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.
  • Fluent English and fluency in the relevant source market language.
  • Strong organizational, multitasking, and time management skills.
  • Experience with Salesforce, Salesloft, Tableau, travel distribution, or API connectivity is advantageous.
  • Existing network within the travel industry is a plus.

At HBX Group, we believe that diversity drives innovation and makes travel a force for good.

We're committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued and respected, embracing different backgrounds, perspectives and talents. Join us and be part of a team where diversity and equal opportunities really do make a difference.

You will have the opportunity to work for a company that is going through significant change in becoming the world´s leading travel services provider. We are looking for people that are ready to ride the wave in this exciting journey.

As well as an attractive benefits package you will be able to work:

  • Within an innovative, engaging and multicultural environment.

  • Have the opportunity to build strong and lasting business relationships and friendships from around the world.

  • Have the opportunity in developing your career locally or within one of our beautiful working locations across the globe.
