jobs.excerpt: We’re hiring an executive coach for Hendrik (CEO of Sharpist) for the next 12+ months.
jobs.description:
We’re hiring an executive coach for Hendrik (CEO of Sharpist) for the next 12+ months.

This is a high-bar search.

We are looking for the top tier — not “good fit,” but the best operator-coach we can find in the market.

Context

Hendrik is leading Sharpist through a category-defining transformation — from a profitable, stable coaching platform into an AI-driven category bet in professional development. The next 12 months will determine whether Sharpist becomes a generational company or a successful European HR-tech player. Hendrik needs to operate at a fundamentally higher altitude to lead it: setting missions rather than running them, building systems that win without him, stepping out of operational work that has historically defined his contribution.

The coach is one of the most important hires of this transformation. They are the intellectual sparring partner who makes the shift in Hendrik’s leadership actually stick.

Non-negotiables

  • C-level operating experience in enterprise SaaS, through the 10M+ ARR scale phase. Founder, CEO, COO, or equivalent. Not earlier-stage, not adjacent industries, not advisor-only careers. They have personally lived the altitude shift we’re hiring them to coach through.

  • Expert coach, primary craft. Trained, certified, actively practicing. Coaching is what they do now — not advisory work with coaching on the side, not “operator who coaches.” We want the coaching craft to lead, with operating depth as the foundation.

  • Track record at the altitude we’re targeting. Has coached founders or CEOs through similar inflection points. Can name them (under NDA). References from current or recent coachees at this level are required.

What we are not looking for

  • Generalist executive coaches without enterprise SaaS context

  • Operators-turned-advisors with strong opinions on what Hendrik should do

  • Wellness, life, or holistic coaches

  • ICF-credential-only coaches without operating depth

  • Anyone who would treat this as “another engagement” rather than the work of a transformation

Focus areas

  • Moving from leader-of-leads to true CEO altitude — football manager mode, not player

  • Building a personal operating system away from task-list-driven work

  • Interrupting the default failure mode of leaning into operational work when stress rises

  • Designing the team architecture around Hendrik — firefighter roles, accountability anchors, ownership transfer

  • Increasing leverage and consequentiality with the leadership team

  • Sustainable energy management

  • Sparring on strategic questions through coaching, not prescription

Logistics

  • Engagement: ongoing, likely 2-4 sessions per month

  • Format: strong preference to deliver via the Sharpist platform (Hendrik is the CEO; using our own product is non-negotiable as a signal and as research)

  • Geography: irrelevant — we want the best person globally

  • Language: English working language

Search posture

This is not a posting. This is an active, high-touch search. We expect to:

  • Source from operator and founder networks, not coaching directories

  • Vet against the non-negotiables ruthlessly — most candidates will not clear the bar

  • Run multiple candidates in parallel rather than evaluating one at a time

  • Move fast once we find the right person — top-tier coaches at this level get booked

  • The right candidate is rare. We are looking for the AAA+ in the market, not the best of who applies.

Requirements

A first conversation with Hendrik should answer:

  • Did they hold a C-level role in enterprise SaaS through the 10M+ ARR scale-up — verifiable?

  • Is coaching their primary craft today, with operating experience as foundation rather than substitute?

  • Do they hold space and let Hendrik find answers, or do they advise and prescribe?

  • Would Hendrik genuinely want to spend two sessions a month with this person for the next 12 months?

  • Are they hungry for this engagement specifically, or treating it as one of many?

The last question matters most. We want someone who, after the first conversation, sees Hendrik and Sharpist as the kind of engagement they would prioritize over others.

Highlights

Sharpist is running a high-touch, operator-network search for an AAA+ coach—C-level enterprise SaaS (10M+ ARR) and coaching-first craft.

About Perle

Perle is an AI infrastructure company building expert-driven training data, evaluation systems, and applied AI products for the world's leading labs and enterprises. Headquartered in San Francisco with experts across more than forty markets, we specialize in the work that requires real human judgment: domain expertise, linguistic nuance, and cultural fidelity that generic data vendors cannot deliver.

Imagine earning extra money without changing a thing about your day. No second shift, no commute, no time away from the work or the life you already have. You film what you are already doing, and you get paid for it.

Perle is building the data that teaches AI and robotics how real people move, work, and get things done. To do that, we need video recorded from a first-person point of view: the world as you see it, through a small camera mounted on a lightweight headstrap. We are looking for contributors across the US, Canada, and Latin America to capture everyday footage and turn their ordinary routines into real income.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

The role is simple: you wear a headstrap with your phone, press record, and go about your day. The footage is captured hands-free from your perspective, so you can keep both hands on whatever you are doing.

Contributors record everyday activities and real work. That includes things like:

  • Household life: doing tasks around the house, cooking, cleaning, organizing, repairs, and other daily routines.
  • On the job: filming while you do your actual job, whether you work in manufacturing, roofing, construction, a restaurant kitchen, a warehouse, or any other hands-on trade.
  • Everyday activities: the small, ordinary moments that make up a normal day, captured naturally as they happen.

There is no script and no acting. The whole point is authentic, real footage of real life. If you can do your job and your daily tasks, you can do this.

Why This Is Worth Your Time

  • Earn while you already work: Record while you work or while you handle things at home. Your day does not change; you just capture it.
  • Total flexibility: There are no fixed shifts. You decide when to record and how much. The more quality footage you submit, the more you earn.
  • Real, steady income: Pay is competitive and varies by region. You are compensated for every hour of accepted footage you deliver.
  • We cover your gear: Perle provides a budget to purchase the headstrap you need to get started, so the equipment is covered.
  • Be part of the future: The work you submit helps train the next generation of AI and robotics. Your everyday routine becomes part of something much bigger.

What You'll Need

  • Location: You must be based in the United States, Canada, or a Latin American country. This role is open to these regions only.
  • Age: You must be 18 years or older.
  • A supported phone: You need one of the following: iPhone 11 or newer, Google Pixel 6 or newer, or Samsung Galaxy S21 or newer. A supported phone is required to capture footage.
  • Willingness to wear a headstrap: You should be comfortable wearing a lightweight headstrap while you work or move around the house. Perle provides a budget so you can purchase one.
  • Around 10 hours a week: A minimum of 10 hours of recorded footage per week is preferred. You are free to record more, and consistency helps you earn more.

How It Works

Step 1 Apply and get approved

Submit your application and confirm you have a supported phone. Once you are approved, we will get you set up.

Step 2 Get your headstrap

We provide a budget to purchase the headstrap. You mount your phone, and you are ready to record hands-free.

Step 3 Record your day

Press record and go about your work and your routine. Capture at least 10 hours of footage a week, on your own schedule.

Step 4 Submit and get paid

Upload your footage through the app. Once it is reviewed and accepted, you are paid for every hour delivered.

Your Data Is Safe With Us

Everything you record is submitted through a dedicated app, which is built to be fully compliant and private. Your footage is encrypted and handled securely from the moment you upload it.

  • One secure channel: Footage is submitted only through the official app. Nothing is shared publicly or posted anywhere.
  • Private by design: Your personal information and your recordings are protected and anonymised and not shared.
  • Fully compliant: The app follows strict data compliance and security standards, so your data stays secure at every step.

Ready to Start Earning?

If you are based in the US, Canada, or Latin America and you want to turn your everyday routine into extra income, we want to hear from you. Whether you are on a roof, in a kitchen, on a factory floor, or just getting things done at home, your day is worth something.

jobs.description:
Software Engineer, Distributed Systems (Core)

Company: Hightouch
Location: Remote (United States or Canada)
Compensation: $180,000 - $320,000 + competitive equity
Employment Type: Full-time
Visa Sponsorship: Visa transfers (can sponsor most visas)

About Hightouch

Hightouch pioneered the Composable Customer Data Platform (CDP), which lets companies use their own data warehouse to collect, prepare and activate customer data for marketing personalization and business operations. Its AI Decisioning platform lets marketers set goals and guardrails that AI agents use to personalize 1:1 customer interactions. Hundreds of companies, including Autotrader, Calendly, Cars.com, Monday.com and PetSmart, rely on it.

Founded in 2018, Hightouch has about 350 people and has raised $320M+ through Series D.

The Role

Hightouch is hiring distributed systems engineers to work on the syncing engine that customers and other engineering teams rely on to move massive amounts of customer data. You will apply expertise in distributed systems, performance optimization and troubleshooting across a multi-cloud, multi-region infrastructure that serves a global customer base. Engineers get very high ownership: you deliver projects start to finish, work directly with customers on their hardest scaling problems and shape what the team works on.

What You Will Do

  • Speed up syncs of large data volumes to destinations like Facebook and Snapchat by optimizing every part of the sync process.
  • Extend batch syncing into real-time streaming syncs from sources such as webhooks and queues.
  • Find and remove scaling and reliability bottlenecks and architect for the next order of magnitude of growth.
  • Evolve the Personalization API, a low-latency caching layer over data warehouses serving sub-30ms p90 responses at millions of QPS.
  • Extend the multi-region, multi-cloud backend to new regions to meet customer data-residency requirements.

What You Bring

  • 7+ years as a software engineer with deep distributed systems work
  • Staff-level scope with fast promotion history at high-growth startups (Series A to E)
  • Very strong systems design fundamentals and understanding of how large-scale distributed systems behave
  • Built event collection or data streaming services that power critical systems (message queues, Kafka, SQL databases, Kubernetes, Docker)
  • Owned systems through orders-of-magnitude growth
  • A pure backend focus (this is not a full-stack, data engineering or DevOps role)
  • Excellent communication and fast learning

Nice to Have

  • Built data sync engines moving terabytes per day
  • Work close to the infrastructure layer; understands how tools like Spark, Flink and Kafka are built
  • Degree from a top computer science program

Interview Process

Recruiter screen (30 min), hiring manager interview (30 min), system design screen (45 min), system design interview (90 min), final call.

Tech Stack

Distributed systems, Kafka, message queues, SQL databases, Kubernetes, Docker, multi-cloud

administrators, and alternative fund managers.

fund administrators, and hedge funds who hold a wide range of public and private securities and general ledger transactions. The DMS plays a critical role in ensuring historical data is transferred efficiently and reconciled with official records.

Our Product

multi-family offices, fund administrators, private equity firms, and hedge funds.

Responsibilities

  • Apply expert Excel and related database programming/management skills to export and organize data from legacy systems for import into FundCount.

Technical Skills

Spreadsheets & Data Automation

Databases & Querying

jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara’s Revenue Accounting team owns how revenue is recognized, reported, and controlled for Samsara’s Connected Operations Platform. As our Revenue Accounting Manager, you will lead the contract review process that turns complex, non-standard customer agreements into defensible ASC 606 conclusions, and ensure deliverables are accurate, automated, and audit-ready. This is a high-visibility role that sits at the intersection of Accounting, Sales, Legal, and Deal Desk — you will help shape deals before they are signed, not just account for them afterward.

You will report to the Director of Revenue Accounting, partnering daily with Deal Desk, Legal, Sales, Revenue Operations, and our external auditors. The work balances technical depth — ASC 606 judgment on novel deal structures — with operational leverage: automating the manual work out of our close and our controls.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except Alaska, Austin Metro, Boulder Metro, California, Chicago Metro, Connecticut, Dallas Metro, Denver Metro, Houston Metro, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Rhode Island, Seattle Metro, and Washington, D.C.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
  • You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. Youwill be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the Contract Review process end-to-end: lead the team to evaluate non-standard and complex customer contracts, determine the appropriate ASC 606 treatment, and document technical accounting positions in memos that stand up to auditor, leadership, and SEC-reporting scrutiny.
  • Drive automation and enhancement of existing processes and controls: strategize, scope and lead improvements to revenue systems, close activities, and control design — from business case through go-live — eliminating manual effort while improving accuracy and timeliness.
  • Partner with Sales, Legal, and Deal Desk teams during contract negotiations to structure deals and optimize revenue outcomes, advising on terms that affect revenue timing, classification, and presentation before agreements are signed.
  • Own the revenue control environment and the external audit relationship: design, rationalize and optimize SOX controls as the business evolves, set the standard for audit-ready evidence, and guide technical conclusions directly with internal and external auditors.
  • Set precedent on complex, ambiguous revenue issues that require in-depth evaluation of variable factors (material right options, variable consideration, contract modifications), determining the methods and procedures to apply where precedent does not yet exist.
  • Build AI-enabled routines across revenue workstreams — contract review triage, memo drafting, reconciliation and anomaly detection, and audit-support preparation — while setting clear guardrails for quality, privacy, and where human accounting judgment must remain explicit.
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices
  • Hire, develop and lead an inclusive, engaged, and high performing team

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 8+ years of progressive accounting experience, including revenue recognition under ASC 606 at a public company, a high-growth technology company, or in public accounting.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
  • Experience reviewing customer contracts and documenting technical revenue recognition positions in written accounting memos.
  • Experience improving or automating accounting processes and controls, including hands-on work in an ERP or revenue subledger (for example NetSuite, Zuora, or RevPro).
  • Experience owning SOX controls and supporting internal and external audits.
  • Experience leading, managing, or mentoring accountants.

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Active CPA license, or CPA eligibility.
  • Big 4 or national public accounting experience, with technical revenue or SEC reporting exposure.
  • Experience in a hardware-plus-software or SaaS business with multi-element arrangements spanning devices, subscriptions, and professional services.
  • Experience partnering with Deal Desk, Legal, and Sales on deal structuring and non-standard commercial terms.
  • Experience implementing or upgrading a revenue automation or contract lifecycle tool, or leading a revenue system migration.
  • A track record of writing accounting positions on novel deal structures that were adopted as company policy.
  • Experience applying AI or analytics tooling to reduce manual accounting work and strengthen controls.
  • Strong written communication — able to make a technical conclusion legible to non-accountants in Sales, Legal, and leadership.

Please note that base pay offered may vary depending on factors including your city of residence, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This role is also eligible for an initial RSU grant with no vesting cliff, and ongoing refresh opportunities tied to performance, subject to plan terms and conditions. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

$107,240—$153,200 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Job Description: Chief Financial Crimes Officer (CFCO)

Industry: Banking, Financial Services, Insurance, Investment

Job Type: Full-Time

Reporting To: Chief Risk Officer (CRO) / Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) / Board Risk & Compliance Committee

Job Summary

The Chief Financial Crimes Officer (CFCO) is responsible for leading the organization's enterprise-wide financial crime prevention framework, including Anti-Money Laundering (AML), Counter-Terrorist Financing (CFT), fraud prevention, sanctions compliance, and anti-bribery & corruption programs.

This role ensures the organization is protected from financial crime risks while maintaining full compliance with regulatory requirements and international standards. The CFCO plays a critical role in safeguarding the organization's integrity, reputation, and operational resilience.

Key Responsibilities

1. Financial Crime Strategy & Governance

Develop and implement a comprehensive financial crime risk management strategy

Establish governance frameworks covering AML, fraud, sanctions, and anti-corruption

Align financial crime programs with enterprise risk and compliance strategies

Promote a strong financial crime compliance culture

2. AML/CFT & Sanctions Compliance

Oversee AML/CFT programs, including KYC, CDD, EDD, and transaction monitoring

Ensure compliance with international standards (e.g., FATF) and local regulations

Manage sanctions screening and compliance frameworks

Ensure timely reporting of suspicious activities (STR/SAR)

3. Fraud Risk Management

Oversee fraud prevention, detection, and investigation frameworks

Implement controls to minimize internal and external fraud risks

Leverage advanced analytics and monitoring tools

Coordinate fraud response and recovery efforts

4. Financial Crime Detection & Investigations

Lead investigations into suspicious transactions and financial crime activities

Ensure proper escalation and reporting to regulators and authorities

Collaborate with law enforcement and financial intelligence units (FIUs)

Maintain robust case management and documentation processes

5. Regulatory Compliance & Reporting

Ensure compliance with all financial crime-related regulations

Manage regulatory inspections, audits, and reporting obligations

Maintain audit-ready documentation and controls

Monitor regulatory developments and adapt frameworks accordingly

6. Technology & Analytics

Oversee financial crime technology platforms (AML, fraud detection, sanctions screening)

Implement AI/ML-based monitoring and analytics tools

Enhance detection capabilities through data-driven insights

Drive digital transformation in financial crime management

7. Training & Awareness

Develop and deliver financial crime training programs

Promote awareness of AML, fraud, and compliance risks

Ensure employees understand reporting obligations and procedures

Foster a culture of vigilance and accountability

8. Stakeholder & Regulatory Engagement

Act as the primary liaison with regulators, FIUs, and law enforcement

Provide financial crime insights to executive leadership and Board

Collaborate with risk, compliance, audit, and business units

Represent the organization in industry forums

9. Leadership & Team Management

Lead and develop financial crime compliance teams

Establish performance standards and KPIs

Foster a culture of integrity and accountability

Support talent development and succession planning

Key Requirements

Education

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Finance, Law, Business Administration, or related field

Professional certifications such as CAMS, CFE, ICA, or equivalent are highly preferred

Experience

12–18+ years of experience in financial crime, AML, fraud, compliance, or risk roles

Proven experience in senior financial crime leadership roles (e.g., CFCO, Head of Financial Crime, AML/Fraud Leader)

Strong experience in banking, financial services, insurance, or investment sectors

Skills & Competencies

Deep knowledge of AML/CFT, fraud, sanctions, and anti-corruption frameworks

Strong analytical and investigative skills

Expertise in financial crime detection and prevention technologies

Leadership and team management

Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement

High ethical standards and attention to detail

Ability to manage complex regulatory environments

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Reduction in financial crime incidents and losses

Compliance with AML/CFT and financial crime regulations

Effectiveness of detection and monitoring systems

Timeliness and accuracy of regulatory reporting

Audit and regulatory inspection outcomes

Employee awareness and training completion

Preferred Attributes

Experience in multinational or highly regulated financial institutions

Exposure to advanced analytics, AI/ML, and regtech solutions

Strong relationships with regulators and law enforcement

Ability to manage complex financial crime risks

Compensation & Benefits

Competitive executive salary

Performance-based incentives

Executive benefits and allowances

jobs.description:
We are hiring a General Counsel, reporting to the Chief Operating Officer (COO). This role leads Canonical’s global Legal and Compliance function.

This is a unique opportunity for an exceptional and commercially-minded senior lawyer to lead the legal and compliance function of a profitable, fast-growing technology company that is privately held with the intention to list on a public exchange. We’re looking for someone with genuine fluency in the software industry and in open source dynamics, who can translate that insight into clear positions on licensing, commercial contracts and risk, and hands-on execution.

Reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer, you will own Canonical's legal, regulatory and governance posture and lead a distributed team across EMEA and the Americas. Your primary challenge will be to continue building both the team and the architecture: a management layer across two regions, and the governance, contracting and controls a public company needs, in an environment that regularly does things the industry has not done before. You will work closely with our product and engineering teams on licensing and IP questions, with the security function on customer assurance, and you will advise the Board and its committees directly.

In our selection process, we prioritize intellect and judgement alongside depth of practice. We are looking for someone with a strong academic background, an active licence to practice, and demonstrable exposure to a multilayered global operational environment.

Location: This role will be based remotely in EMEA time zones, with an option to be office based in London, UK.

The role entails

  • Leading the global Legal and Compliance function: setting it's structure, standards and priorities across EMEA and the Americas.
  • Building and managing a management capability: hire and develop managers, set objectives, review performance against a clear bar, and address under-performance directly.
  • Setting the operating cadence of the function: intake and prioritization of legal work, service expectations with internal clients, and reporting on workload and risk to the leadership team.
  • Owning public-market readiness on the legal side: corporate governance, group and entity structure, delegated authority, policies, disclosure controls and records, in partnership with Finance.
  • Advising the CEO, COO, CFO and the Board, and supporting in Board and committee meetings.
  • Owning the commercial contracting framework: standard templates, negotiating positions, and a deviation and escalation process that makes commitments visible before they are signed.
  • Leading intellectual property and open source licensing strategy, including copyleft, trademark and the terms on which Ubuntu and our products are distributed.
  • Owning the global compliance programme: data protection and privacy, export controls and trade compliance, anti-bribery and corruption, competition and AI regulation.
  • Managing litigation, disputes and regulatory engagement, together with the external counsel panel, its budget and its quality.
  • Advising on M&A, partnerships, strategic alliances and financing as the company grows.

What we are looking for in you

  • An exceptional academic track record from both high school and university.
  • A degree in law, or equivalent, and an active licence to practice in an EMEA or Americas jurisdiction.
  • Substantial senior in-house experience in a global technology or software business.
  • Proven experience leading a distributed legal team, including managing managers across regions and time zones.
  • A track record of setting and holding a high performance bar: hiring well, developing people, and dealing with under performance directly rather than waiting it out.
  • Experience building or restructuring an in-house legal function, including deciding what is retained, delegated and sent to external counsel.
  • Technology related experience of:
    • negotiating and owning commercial technology contracts, including enterprise software and subscriptions, channel and reseller agreements, hardware manufacturer agreements, cloud and services
    • advising on open source licensing, including permissive and copyleft licences, and familiarity with how open source communities operate.
  • Experience of, or demonstrable readiness for, public company governance: listing preparation, board and committee support, disclosure and controls.
  • Depth in at least two of: data protection and privacy, IP and trademark, export controls and trade, competition, or disputes.
  • Confidence to respectfully speak up, exchange feedback, hold colleagues accountable, and share ideas without hesitation.
  • Professional written and spoken English with excellent drafting and presentation skills.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills, curiosity, flexibility, and accountability.
  • International travel two to four times a year for company events up to two weeks long.

Nice-to-have skills

  • Experience taking a company through an IPO, or practicing as counsel inside a listed company.
  • A technical or engineering background, or fluency in how software is built and shipped.
  • Experience of a subscription or recurring-revenue business model.
  • Experience building or restructuring an in-house legal function.
  • A qualification in more than one jurisdiction.

What we offer colleagues

We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

  • Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person.

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. We are founder-led, profitable, and growing.

Powered by worldwide distributed collaboration since our inception in 2004, we believe tech and business leadership can emerge anywhere. We have no central headquarters. Most of us work from home, but we are exceptionally disciplined about this. We have very high expectations of all colleagues, and are champions of excellence. Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer

jobs.description:
About Juno

Juno leverages collective bargaining power to secure better student loan rates for students. With 290,000+ members and over $2B in negotiated loan volume, we've proven that group buying works. We are the most popular way to pay for the world's top graduate programs, and we're looking for someone to own the healthcare channels that reach our members at the moments that decide whether they borrow with us.

The Problem

Federal lending reforms have created a significant market shift. In July 2026, new caps on federal graduate loans, including the elimination of Grad PLUS for new students, came into effect, leaving millions of students with significant funding gaps. Students need transparent, competitive private options: exactly what Juno provides.

Your Mission

We're seeking a leader to own full-funnel growth across our healthcare portfolio: pharmacy, physical therapy, veterinary medicine, and adjacent programs. This is a portfolio role: you'll run several markets at once, decide where the next dollar of effort goes, and build repeatable playbooks that work across them.

You'll build the playbook for reaching hundreds of programs across these fields and establish Juno as the go-to resource for financing a healthcare degree.

What You'll Do

  • Own the healthcare portfolio: Build and execute GTM strategy across pharmacy, PT, vet, and adjacent programs, prioritize across markets based on size and momentum, hit growth targets, and drive Juno member growth.
  • Scale distribution through partnerships:
    • Negotiate national deals with key organizations that can help reach our target market
    • Activate campus-based chapters with turnkey playbooks
    • Partner with test prep companies, professional associations, and content creators in each field
    • Run targeted campaigns aligned to application cycles
  • Build a campus ambassador network: Recruit, train, and manage high-performing students across pharmacy, PT, vet, and adjacent programs with clear KPIs and incentives.
  • Talk to members directly: Talk to students directly throughout the cycle: calls, email, DMs, and campus visits. You should know the top five reasons a pharmacy or PT student with a rate offer never submits an application because you've heard them first-hand, not because a dashboard told you.
  • Be the expert students trust: Become fluent in how graduate borrowing actually works (federal vs. private, what drives a rate, cosigners, in-school deferral, refinancing, and what changed under the new caps) and be the person who can give a P1 or a first-year DPT student a straight answer.
  • Drive cross-functional initiatives: Partner with product on feature development, collaborate with the CX/client happiness team, and ensure messaging compliance.
  • Manage operations and analytics: Forecast pipeline, track cohort performance, optimize CAC/LTV, and manage budget allocation.
  • Own the funnel: Partner with senior leadership to own waitlist growth → loan origination: landing pages, A/B tests, content, webinars, email/SMS, and event cycles aligned to application, admissions, and financial aid timelines.

What We Offer

  • Compensation: $150k-$250k, including performance upside tied to growth milestones. Top performers will exceed this range.
  • Benefits: Comprehensive health, dental, vision, and retirement matching.

What We're Looking For

  • Background: Typically 3-5+ years, or an outlier track record (e.g., you scaled a campus network, ran national org programming, or built a zero-to-one motion).
    • Preference for experience in professional services, management consulting, investment banking, or high-growth startups
    • Preference for an owner-operator who has owned a number in growth, BD, marketplaces, fintech, edtech, or campus-scale programs
  • Ownership of a number, end to end: You'll carry the healthcare portfolio's funded-loan target and the conversion rates underneath it. You're comfortable being both the person who explains a miss and the person who fixes it.
  • Bias to action: Ship experiments frequently, instrument attribution, and close loops with lender relations and compliance.
  • Fluency with your own data: You can find where students stall between a rate offer and a submitted application, and make the case for a fix with evidence rather than instinct.
  • Relationship-building that compounds: Schools, student organizations, ambassadors, admissions communities, and lender partners. You're equally comfortable on a call with a target B2B partner and in a group chat with students.
  • Zero-to-one comfort: There is no existing playbook for this vertical. You'll write it, and you find that exciting rather than daunting.
  • Comfort with seasonality: Our year has a peak. You plan for it months ahead and go all-in when it lands.
  • Tenacity: We work as hard as it takes to achieve our targets.

The X-Factor

  • You're hungry: Ready to own outcomes, not just make recommendations.
  • You're scrappy: You'll do whatever it takes to win.
  • You're magnetic: You can recruit and inspire great people.
  • You think in systems: You'd rather build the process once than do the thing by hand ten times.

Why Join Juno?

  • Real impact: Help hundreds of thousands of students get access to the lowest rates on the market.
  • Market timing: Federal aid changes create a massive tailwind for growth.
  • Proven model: $2B+ negotiated and 290K+ members. Product-market fit achieved.

Independent Contractor | Fully Remote | 8–16 Clinical Hours per Week

Join a practice built around psychologists.

Affiliates are independent contractors who provide between 8 and 16 clinical hours per week, entirely via telehealth. You choose a consistent schedule and clinical commitment that works for your life; PSM provides the referrals, systems, and administrative infrastructure surrounding your practice.

This can be an ideal position for psychologists who want to maintain meaningful clinical work alongside another professional role, teaching, consulting, family or personal commitments, semi-retirement, or simply a schedule that leaves room for life outside of work.

What PSM Provides

  • A flexible schedule: Maintain a consistent caseload of 8–16 clinical hours per week.

We welcome psychologists who are strong clinicians and value autonomy, collaboration, professional growth, and evidence-based practice. Our psychologists are often strong generalists who also bring particular areas of specialization, clinical interests, or expertise.

Our affiliates have the freedom to maintain a limited clinical schedule while benefiting from strong referrals, sophisticated administrative support, continuing education, consultation, multidisciplinary colleagues, and an organization with an established reputation for high-quality psychological care.

jobs.description:
Location: This position may be performed remotely, but requires the flexibility and willingness to travel as needed.

The Opportunity

Praxis is hiring a Director, Clinical Systems & Data. You would lead the strategy, roadmap, and delivery of the clinical systems and data capabilities that support Praxis’s clinical development and study operations. This includes translating clinical priorities and study milestones into clear technology priorities, making thoughtful investment and sequencing decisions, and driving delivery with urgency and accountability.

Within IT, you will own the clinical systems and data capability while partnering closely with Clinical Operations, Data & Analytics, Quality, Regulatory, and external technology providers. The role calls for creating clarity across functions, establishing decision rights, resolving competing priorities, and ensuring the systems and data supporting our clinical programs are reliable, scalable, secure, and fit for purpose.

You will provide leadership across clinical data engineering, data platform architecture, clinical systems delivery, and related validation activities. At the same time, you’ll stay close to the technology and the work—challenging designs, troubleshooting issues, escalating when needed, and applying sound judgment to keep delivery moving.

You will also help shape how Praxis uses clinical technology and data to work better. You’ll move the organization from fragmented or static workflows toward governed, reusable data products, analytics, and practical AI-enabled tools that help teams make better decisions and work more effectively. Success will include building an operating model that scales with the organization, strengthens inspection readiness and operational resilience, and reduces dependency on individual contributors.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Own the clinical systems and data strategy and roadmap; translate clinical development priorities and study milestones into sequenced investments, clear priorities, and measurable outcomes.
  • Lead and develop the clinical data engineering and data platform capability, including architecture, data flows, integrations, access controls, data quality, cloud platforms, and reusable data products across clinical systems.
  • Create clarity across IT and functional teams by establishing decision rights, aligning stakeholders on requirements and acceptance decisions, resolving competing demands, and driving timely decisions.
  • Partner with Clinical Operations and other functional teams to improve the reliability, usability, and scalability of clinical systems and technology-enabled study workflows.
  • Lead the evolution from fragmented or static workflows toward governed, reusable analytics and practical AI-enabled tools that create meaningful value for clinical teams.
  • Lead system implementations, integrations, enhancements, upgrades, issue resolution, and transition to ongoing support; coordinate internal teams, vendors, and implementation partners across dependencies, risks, and milestones.
  • Own the IT relationship with clinical technology vendors and service providers; establish service expectations, evaluate platform choices, manage performance, and inform investment and renewal decisions.
  • Partner with Quality and functional owners on risk-based computerized systems assurance and validation, including requirements, test strategy, traceability, validation evidence, vendor deliverables, remediation, and inspection readiness.
  • Establish and maintain strong standards for system lifecycle management, change control, access governance, security, data stewardship, incident management, business continuity, and operational resilience.
  • Provide hands-on technical leadership when needed, including architecture reviews, troubleshooting, vendor escalation, and evaluation of new technologies; build a durable operating model that enables the clinical organization to scale.

Qualifications and Key Success Factors

  • 10+ years of relevant experience across clinical systems, clinical data platforms, data engineering, technology delivery, or related disciplines, including leadership of complex cross-functional initiatives.
  • Experience supporting pharmaceutical or biotechnology clinical development and delivering technology or data capabilities in a regulated environment.
  • Strong understanding of the clinical technology ecosystem, including data integrations, cloud platforms, data architecture, analytics, and the operational needs of clinical teams.
  • Experience with computerized systems validation, computer software assurance, GxP expectations, change control, data integrity, and inspection readiness.
  • Ability to translate clinical and business priorities into practical roadmaps, investment decisions, delivery plans, and measurable outcomes, while effectively managing technology vendors and budgets.
  • Technical fluency across data flows, APIs, integration patterns, cloud data platforms, and analytics tools, with the ability to challenge designs, identify dependencies, and guide delivery.
  • Experience leading requirements definition, testing, user acceptance, change management, training, and transition to ongoing support.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead technical teams and influence cross-functional stakeholders without relying solely on formal authority. Creates clarity, builds trust, and holds teams accountable for outcomes.
  • A strong ownership mindset, with the ability to step into ambiguity, surface risks early, make decisions with appropriate urgency, and stay engaged through resolution.
    Comfort balancing speed with rigor, particularly in regulated environments, and knowing when to move quickly, when additional diligence is needed, and how to build controls that enable both.
  • Clear, direct communication and the ability to adapt to different audiences while remaining technically engaged and contributing hands-on when needed.
    Alignment with Praxis values of Trust, Ownership, Curiosity, and Results, demonstrated through how you lead, make decisions, collaborate, and deliver.
  • The physical and mental requirements of our roles include but are not limited to regular use of a computer, devices or other office equipment, clear communication, and occasional movement. You’ll need comfort with screen work, basic hand coordination, and focus. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these functions.
Annualized Base Salary
$205,000—$229,000 USD

Compensation & BenefitsAt Praxis, we believe that taking care of our people (and their people) is important, so we provide a world class benefits package to help you thrive.  This includes 99% of the premium paid for medical, dental and vision plans. We also provide company-paid life insurance, AD&D, disability benefits, and voluntary plans to personalize your coverage. Thinking about the future?  We match dollar-for-dollar up to 6% on eligible 401(k) contributions and sweeten the deal with long-term stock incentives and ESPP.  We provide a discretionary quarterly bonus, an extremely flexible wellness benefit, generous PTO, paid holidays and company-wide shutdowns.  Not to mention, you'll also be joining a phenomenal crew of colleagues who are smart, engaged and inspiring.  We aim high, collaborate hard, and produce results.  Let’s achieve the impossible together!

Company Overview

Praxis Precision Medicines is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company translating genetic insights into the development of therapies for central nervous system disorders characterized by neuronal imbalance. At Praxis we share a common vision of reshaping the human condition into a more freeing and fulfilled existence by developing high impact medicines for patients and families affected by and living with complex brain disorders. Our core Values of Trust, Ownership, Curiosity and Results are foundational to every aspect of our business and are exemplified by each and every one of our team members.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion
Guided by our core values, at Praxis Precision Medicines, Inc. we continue to DARE FOR MORE® to advance, promote, and champion diversity, equity, and inclusion by encouraging individuals to bring their authentic selves and perspectives to work each day. We are an equal opportunity employer and committed to providing opportunities to all qualified applicants without regard to race, religious creed, color, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, sexual orientation, disability, genetics, military service and veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

jobs.title: Global Africa Employer Partnerships Manager (12 Months Fixed-Term/Remote)
jobs.excerpt: ABOUT GENERATION At Generation, we believe in the power of employment to change lives.
jobs.description:
ABOUT GENERATION

At Generation, we believe in the power of employment to change lives. We are a global nonprofit organization that supports adults to achieve economic mobility through employment. Generation trains and places adult learners of all ages into careers that are otherwise inaccessible, working in partnership with governments, employers, and other system actors. We also conduct original research and share data insights on high-priority global workforce transition topics to inform decision-making by workforce system stakeholders. Launched in 2015, Generation comprises a global hub (Generation You Employed, or GYE) and a network of in-country affiliates. To date, the network has 150,000+ graduates and 23,000+ employers across 50 professions and 17 countries.

When learners join Generation, 91% are unemployed, of which nearly half are long-term unemployed. Three months after completing our program, graduates have a 78% job placement rate, rising to 88% within six months. Of our employed graduates, 79% are hired by repeat employers who have previously hired Generation graduates, and 89% are in jobs directly related to the profession for which we have trained them. Employed graduates immediately earn an average of 3-4X their previous earnings. Two to five years after graduation, 77% of our alumni from upper-middle income countries continue to meet their daily financial needs and 63% can save for the future. To date, Generation’s global graduates have earned more than $1.9 billion in wages. Generation graduates typically have a secondary school background, 52% are female, 28% have dependents, and the majority identify with underrepresented communities in their country.

JOB OBJECTIVES

Generation operates across multiple African countries. Currently anchored in Ghana and Kenya, with strong ambition to deepen its impact, expand into new markets, and build more financially sustainable operating models. Over the next two years, Generation seeks to scale multi-country operations to four or more countries, pilot a sector ecosystem model, and establish a trajectory towards earned revenue and reduced donor dependency in Africa.

We are seeking an Africa Employer Partnerships Manager to lead employer engagement across Generation’s Africa portfolio, with a dual focus on:

  1. Securing anchor, multi-country partnerships with multinational employers—particularly in BPO/ITO and digital/tech sectors
  2. Driving employer demand and placement opportunities in new and scaling markets (initially Nigeria, and subsequently Ethiopia, South Africa, and others)

Reporting to the Region CEO for South Asia, Middle East, and Africa (SAMEA), with a dotted-line relationship to the Global Employer Partnerships Director, this role sits at the intersection of commercial growth, strategic partnerships, and market expansion.

This is a high-impact, hands-on role: the successful candidate will both lead complex, enterprise-level partnerships and personally source and close employer relationships in new markets. Over time, the role may involve building and managing a regional employer partnerships team.

This is a 12-month fixed-term employee contract, renewable subject to performance and continued funding, with strong potential for extension and long-term growth.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Strategic Employer Partnerships (Multi-country / MNC focus)

  • Identify, develop, and secure anchor partnerships with multinational employers that can scale across multiple African countries
  • Build and manage enterprise-level relationships, designing partnership models that align with Generation’s programs and employer talent needs
  • Create strategic partnerships that create revenue and help us to further our mission.
  • Collaborate closely with global and regional leadership, as well as country teams in Kenya and Ghana, to align on partnership strategy and delivery
  • Coordinate cross-country engagement with employers to ensure consistency and maximize long-term partnership value

2.Employer Sourcing & Vacancy Generation in New Markets

  • Act as the primary employer partnerships lead in new or early-stage countries (initially Nigeria) where we don’t have local team presence
  • Personally source, engage, and close employers, securing job opportunities for Generation graduates
  • Build a strong pipeline of employers and vacancies aligned to program needs and growth plans
  • Develop and refine the employer partnerships playbook for new market entry

3.Business Development

  • Deliver against defined KPI’s and targets such as new partnerships, opportunities, vacancies, recruitment conversion rates and placements.
  • Build a robust partnerships pipeline to support consistent delivery across multiple markets
  • Develop and refine employer value propositions to drive long-term strategic partnerships
  • Track performance rigorously, providing regular reporting on pipeline and conversion metrics

4.Account Management & Partnership Growth

  • Ensure strong post-placement engagement with employers, including interview processes, feedback loops, and performance tracking
  • Grow and deepen relationships with existing partners to drive repeat hiring and expanded engagement across geographies
  • Act as the point of escalation for complex employer issues across multiple countries
  • Capture and share employer insights to inform program design and employer value proposition

5.International & Remote Work Opportunities

  • Identify and secure international remote work opportunities for Generation graduates across Africa
  • Develop partnerships with global employers that enable cross-border employment pathways, particularly in digital and remote-first roles
  • Collaborate with global teams to align on remote talent strategies and employer requirements

6.Team Leadership & Regional Capability Building

  • Recruit, manage, and develop regional BD / Employer Partnerships Associates as the Africa portfolio grows
  • Set clear targets, manage performance, and build a high-performing regional partnerships function
  • Provide coaching and support to in-country employer partnerships teams where needed, ensuring alignment and knowledge sharing

7.Contribution to Regional & Global Strategy

  • Input into Africa growth strategy, particularly on employer demand, sector focus, and revenue models
  • Contribute to the development of global employer partnerships approaches, tools, and playbooks
  • Represent Generation externally with employers, industry groups, and ecosystem stakeholders across Africa

QUALIFICATIONS

Experience

  • 6–12 years of experience in business development, enterprise sales, partnerships, or employer engagement roles
  • Demonstrated track record of closing partnerships and delivering targets, ideally with large or multinational organizations
  • Experience operating across multiple markets, ideally within Africa
  • Proven ability to build and grow partnerships in new or early-stage markets
  • Experience managing or mentoring team members or associates
  • Experience in workforce development, skills training, recruitment, or related sectors is an advantage, but not required

Knowledge & Skills

  • Strong commercial acumen and ability to structure revenue-generating partnerships
  • Proven experience of developing partnerships across Africa
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to influence senior decision-makers
  • Ability to balance strategic partnership development with hands-on execution
  • Strong pipeline management and organisational skills
  • Understanding of talent management, recruitment, workforce development or HR
  • Ability to operate effectively in a matrixed, multi-country environment
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills

Personal Attributes

  • Entrepreneurial and proactive — comfortable building from scratch in new markets
  • Results-oriented and resilient — driven to meet ambitious targets
  • Collaborative — able to work across global and regional teams
  • Passionate about Generation’s mission and improving employment outcomes for the unemployed or underemployed

We will be in touch with you soon after you submit your application, as long as you have:

  • Submitted a resume & cover letter; and
  • Passion for bicycles with a strong knowledge of bicycle products.
  • Exceptional communication skills in English, both written and verbal.

BikesOnline is committed to creating a diverse environment and is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability or age.

jobs.title: SVP Clinical Development & Global Program Lead, Pancreatic Cancer
jobs.excerpt: Erasca is a clinical-stage precision oncology company focused on discovering, developing and commercializing medicines for the benefit of patients with cancer.
jobs.description:
Erasca is a clinical-stage precision oncology company focused on discovering, developing and commercializing medicines for the benefit of patients with cancer. Our programs take novel approaches to shutting down one of cancer’s most commonly mutated signaling cascades, the RAS/MAPK pathway, which affects approximately 5.5 million lives each year worldwide. The name “Erasca” has an important embedded meaning: it is a contraction of our audacious hope to “erase cancer” that drives our mission and everything that we do on behalf of patients with cancer.

Position Summary: 

Reporting to the Chief Medical Officer, the VP Clinical Development and Global Program Lead (GPL) for GI Cancers will provide medical leadership and oversight of the pancreatic and colorectal cancer development programs and collaborate with the CMO across the Erasca portfolio. Responsibilities will include clinical development strategy, protocol development, registrational strategy and execution, KOL and academic site interactions, competitive landscape diligence, presentation of data, and other clinical deliverables. In addition, the VP will be a hands–on drug developer and will serve as clinical lead and/or medical monitor on individual studies.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Provide medical direction and high-quality scientific and clinical knowledge to guide the strategy and execution of the pancreatic and colorectal cancer programs and contribute to clinical decision making across the Erasca portfolio. Participate in building and maintaining a culture of rigorous data-driven decision making.
  • Lead the clinical development subteam for all studies in GI cancers.
  • Design and implement novel and efficient clinical trials to assess appropriate endpoints.
  • Responsible for leading clinical study subteams, monitoring overall study integrity, and review, interpretation, and communication of safety and efficacy data.
  • Provide overall strategy for clinical aspects of registrational strategies, interactions, and filings. Contribute to global regulatory filings and health authority interactions, including authoring clinical sections for INDs, NDAs and other related documents.
  • Serve as Medical lead on clinical programs and represent Clinical Development on program teams.
  • Partner with Drug Safety to assess the safety profile of compounds.
  • Write or partner in the authoring of medical aspects of core study and regulatory documents including clinical research plans, protocols, investigator brochures, clinical study reports and regulatory submissions.
  • Contribute to the development and review of scientific publications; author manuscripts and collaborate with cross-functional colleagues and thought leaders to meet publication plan objectives.
  • Present at scientific, medical, and regulatory meetings.
  • Maintain a high level of clinical and scientific expertise by reviewing literature, attending medical or scientific meetings, and through personal exchange with thought leaders, investigators, and internal stakeholders and partners.
  • Participate in due diligence or other business development activities.
  • Hire, develop, and mentor a high functioning team of medical directors and clinical scientists.
  • Establish, develop, and maintain relationships across Erasca, particularly with partners and stakeholders in Research and Development.
  • Perform all duties in keeping with the Company’s core values, policies and all applicable regulations.

Required Education and Experience:

  • M.D. degree or equivalent, with subspecialty fellowship training and board certification or eligibility in Oncology or Oncology/Hematology required.
  • 8-10+ years of oncology clinical trial and drug development experience, including extensive experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry. The ideal candidate will bring a combination of clinical practice, academic clinical trials, and industry experience, with both large and small company experience a plus.
  • Experience as the clinical lead on late-stage clinical programs in colorectal, pancreatic, or other GI cancers required.
  • Experience leading or being closely involved in the clinical aspects of a regulatory filing and direct interaction with health authorities required.
  • Exposure to early development and the transition from FIH to registrational trials preferred.
  • Extensive knowledge of clinical trial methodology and the regulatory and compliance requirements governing clinical trials.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate successfully with multiple functions in a matrixed team environment.
  • Executive leadership skills to educate and influence stakeholders and to add value in strategic business planning and decision-making.
  • Effective interpersonal, communication and influencing skills, including excellent writing skills, with the ability to tailor communication style to diverse audiences and situations.

Responsibilities

  • Define radiometric calibration methodology, establishing the standards and procedures used to convert raw instrument signal into calibrated, science-grade measurements.
  • Define geometric calibration methodology, establishing the standards and procedures used to determine and correct the instrument's pointing and geometric accuracy.
  • Define calibration data processing and outputs, partnering with the Infrared Data Product team to ensure calibration artifacts meet downstream product needs.
  • Support ground-calibration test planning, partnering with the Instrument Scientist responsible for Calibration Testing to translate methodology into executable test procedures.

Qualifications

  • Experience turning radiometric or geometric calibration methodology into data processing algorithms that produce calibration products.
  • Strong communication skills, comfortable translating calibration methodology into requirements and test procedures across Instrument Systems, Instrument Assembly, Integration and Test, and Instrument Design.

Nice-to-have Skills

  • Familiarity with ground calibration test infrastructure and procedures.
  • Experience with visible and infrared sensors, and scanner characterization.
  • Experience supporting calibration data validation with downstream data product teams.

Senior Marketing Manager

About Nametag
Nametag is building the future of secure digital identity. Our mission is to protect every human identity to restore trust in the AI era. We bring workforce-grade identity verification into the enterprise to verify the human behind accounts and critical actions. Today, global enterprises use Nametag across their workforce to prevent social engineering and deepfake impersonation attacks.

The Role

Nametag is hiring a Senior Marketing Manager to be one of the primary hands on our content engine; the person who can take a product update, a customer story, or an industry trend and turn it into a blog post, an email, a one-pager, and a social thread. This role leans content: you should be, first and foremost, an excellent writer who's comfortable in a technical B2B space. It's also a generalist role where you'll move across channels and formats rather than owning one lane, which suits someone who wants breadth over deep specialization in any single channel.

Role Overview

As Senior Marketing Manager, you will own a meaningful share of Nametag's day-to-day content output: blog posts, email newsletters, social copy, website updates, sales one-pagers, and event collateral. You'll work closely with Growth Marketing, Product Marketing, Design, Sales, Customer Success, and Channel Partnerships to keep everything on-voice and moving, and you'll often be the person turning someone else's raw material into something customers, prospects, and partners actually read.

What you’ll do

  1. Content Creation & Editorial Ownership
  • Write and edit the majority of Nametag's recurring content: blog posts, thought-leadership articles, email newsletters, and website copy updates.
  • Maintain a consistent voice and terminology across everything you touch, using Nametag's messaging and style guide as the working standard.
  • Turn technical product detail into copy a security, IT, or HR buyer will want to read, without losing accuracy along the way.
  1. Sales & Customer-Facing Collateral
  • Write and refresh customer-facing collateral: one-pagers, solution briefs, and customer stories.
  • Turn customer conversations and Customer Success input into concrete proof points and case studies.
  • Keep collateral current as messaging and product details change, rather than letting outdated one-pagers keep circulating.
  1. Multi-Channel Campaign Support
  • Write copy supporting Growth Marketing's campaigns across email, social, paid, and landing pages.
  • Adapt a single core message across formats and channels so campaigns feel coordinated rather than assembled from parts.
  • Support A/B testing of messaging and creative with fresh copy variants.
  1. Event & Field Marketing Content
  • Produce content supporting Nametag's conference presence and field events: talk-track material, dinner and panel briefs, and pre- and post-event follow-up content.
  • Partner with Channel Partnerships on content for partner-facing events and co-marketing moments.
  1. Editorial Calendar & Cross-Functional Coordination
  • Own and maintain the marketing content calendar, coordinating inputs from Growth Marketing, Product Marketing, Design, and Sales so nothing ships late, off-voice, or duplicated.
  • Flag gaps and inconsistencies in existing content and messaging, and drive them to resolution rather than letting them sit.
  1. Performance & Iteration
  • Track content performance: engagement, email metrics, content-influenced pipeline, in partnership with Growth Marketing, and use it to prioritize what to write next.

What You Bring

We encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply, even if you don't meet every listed qualification. You'll thrive in this role if you bring most of the following:

  • ~8 years in B2B marketing, with some of that time in a content-heavy role: content marketing, editorial, communications, or a marketing generalist role centered on writing.
  • Genuine comfort as a generalist. Someone who'd rather move across several channels well than own one channel deeply.
  • Experience marketing to technical or security-conscious B2B audiences; cybersecurity, IAM, or enterprise IT experience is a strong plus.
  • Ability to turn a customer conversation, a product spec, or a conference talk into content without losing what mattered in translation.
  • Working familiarity with marketing tools such as HubSpot, Google Analytics, and a CMS (Webflow or similar); light design-tool comfort (e.g., Canva) is useful, though this isn't a design role.
  • Strong organizational and project management skills.
  • A strong sense of ownership and a bias toward shipping.+

What We Value

  • Intellectual horsepower. Quickly grasping complex technical and business concepts.
  • Kindness and integrity. Earning trust is central to how we build relationships with customers and colleagues.
  • Bias for action. We move quickly to deliver impact and protect our customers against fast-moving threats.
  • Ownership mindset. You care about uptime and stability the way a founder cares about the product.

Culture & Perks

At Nametag, we believe trust starts with how we treat each other. We're a remote-first team that values autonomy, inclusivity, and collaboration, with regular in-person time to stay connected and innovate together.

ABOUT GENERATION

At Generation, we believe in the power of employment to change lives. We are a global nonprofit organization that supports adults to achieve economic mobility through employment. Generation trains and places adult learners of all ages into careers that are otherwise inaccessible, working in partnership with governments, employers, and other system actors. We also conduct original research and share data insights on high priority global workforce transition topics to inform decision-making by workforce system stakeholders. Launched in 2015, Generation comprises a global hub (Generation You Employed, or GYE) and a network of in-country affiliates. To date, the network has 100,000+ graduates and 11,000+ employers across 46 professions and 17 countries.

When learners join Generation, 91% are unemployed, of which nearly half are long-term unemployed.  Three months after completing our program, graduates have a 78% job placement rate, rising to 88% within six months. Of our employed graduates, 68% are hired by repeat employers who have previously hired Generation graduates, and 89% are in jobs directly related to the profession for which we have trained them. Employed graduates immediately earn an average of 3-4X theirprevious earnings.  Two to five years after graduation, 77% of our alumni from upper-middle income countries continue to meet their daily financial needs and 63% can save for the future. To date, Generation’s global graduates have earned more than $1 billion in wages. Generation graduates typically have a secondary school background, 54% are female, 34% have dependents, and the majority identify with underrepresented communities in their country.

JOB OBJECTIVES

The Multi-country Programme Manager (PM) is accountable for coordinating and scaling Generation's delivery across multiple satellite markets in West and East Africa, with an initial focus on Nigeria, Kenya, and Ethiopia. The role owns multi-country programme design, in-country program coordination and cross-border operational problem-solving. The PM ensures Generation's methodology is delivered consistently across diverse markets while navigating the operational complexities of remote learner mobilization, localized infrastructure support, and distributed job placement pipelines.

This is a high-impact, high-visibility role for someone who thrives on solving coordination challenges at scale, managing remote teams, and building systems that work across multiple countries simultaneously.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Multi-country Programme Coordination

  • Own the end-to-end delivery of multi-country cohorts across satellite markets, ensuring Generation methodology is faithfully implemented, and quality standards are maintained. This includes overseeing local partnership development, Training Service Partner (TSP) relationship management, safeguarding compliance, and in-country Generation representation.

  • Design and refine the multi-country operating model based on lessons learned, testing approaches to address key bottlenecks including dispersed mobilisation, developing local partnerships, localised infrastructure support, cross-border payments, and harmonised data systems.

2. In-country Coordination

  • Manage In-country Coordinators/teams, where existent, in each satellite market (Nigeria, Ethiopia). This includes setting clear expectations and providing performance management.
  • Support In-country Coordinators (where existent) to identify and manage Training Service Providers (TSPs) within their satellite markets, holding TSPs accountable for delivery quality, learner support, and outcome achievement.

3. Cross-border Operational Problem-Solving

  • Navigate and resolve operational challenges unique to multi-country delivery, including cross border learner stipend payments, compliance with local labour and safeguarding regulations, device and connectivity support for remote learners, and harmonized data tracking across Salesforce and other Generation systems.
  • Liaise with Global Finance, Global HR, and the Digital team to implement scalable solutions for cross-border payments and multi-country safeguarding protocols.
  • Develop contingency plans for country-specific risks including political instability, regulatory shifts, currency volatility, and partner non-performance.

4. Strategic Partnership Development

  • Support in the design of partnership and market entry and scale up strategy of multi-country program delivery in line with overall Generation Direct delivery strategy including partnerships, mobilization, learner engagement, and learner support.
  • Identify and cultivate strategic partnerships in satellite markets to support multi-country programme delivery, including local hubs, Training Service Providers, connectivity providers, mobilization partners, grassroot and community-led organisations, government institutions, relevant industry/sector bodies and employer partners.
  • Support In-country Coordinators to represent Generation at local stakeholder convenings, government forums, and employer roundtables, building Generation's brand recognition and credibility in each market.

QUALIFICATIONS

Essential Experience & Skills

  • 5+ years of experience in programme management, operations, or project coordination, ideally within international development, skilling-to-employment, workforce development, or education sectors.
  • Proven track record of managing multi-country or multi-site programmes, with demonstrated ability to coordinate remote teams, navigate cross-border complexities, and maintain quality standards across diverse contexts.

Desirable Experience

  • Exposure to employer engagement, learner mobilisation, or placement functions within skilling or employment programmes.

Personal Attributes

Money is moving onto the internet, and the shift has a name: Open Money. This is money that is open, portable, agentic, and owned by you. Now we're building the operating system for your money: one place to hold, move, grow, and use anything you own. Join a remote-first, global team rebuilding how money works: a problem that touches everyone, every day.

About the role

This role runs the internal posture engine — the risk register, critical control monitoring, evidence, audit operations and GRC tooling. It keeps risk state current so the Lead and the Risk Committee decide from accurate data in the Risk Dashboard and reporting. Drata is the register of record. Named owners close gaps; this role keeps the register, evidence and audit operations current.

Responsibilities

Planning

  • Operate the risk register from the Security Programme threat model: populate, track treatment, record acceptance decisions, follow up owners, and run the exceptions register.
  • Keep the ISMS and security policy library current as part of audit readiness. Draft security standards when commissioned by the Lead.
  • Run Drata as the control and evidence system — Statement of Applicability, framework crosswalk and automation.

Execution

  • Run critical control monitoring: health check-ins, drift flags and Drata automation. Route drift to the SOC. Maintain the evidence file for Lead assessments and independent internal audit.
  • Feed threat-assessment findings into the register and confidence ratings. Track which required assessments are current.
  • Lead audit coordination and preparation: ISO 27001 and SOC 2 logistics, ISMS readiness, team prep, management-review pack, and customer due-diligence questionnaires.
  • Coordinate the control register for external testing (red team, tabletop, pentest). Run security awareness and weekly alerts.

Tracking and evaluating performance

  • Track residual risk, exceptions and gap-closure against appetite. Exceptions expire and are reported; the underlying requirement stays in force.
  • Report register state and evidence health so the Lead and Risk Committee work from one view.

Achieving overall defined performance

  • Be accountable for a current, defensible posture engine — register, evidence and audit operations.
  • Ensure Drata collects evidence continuously, with automated evidence where coverage exists.

Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience running a risk register, control library and audit cycle (ISO 27001 and/or SOC 2).
  • Comfortable with GRC platforms (Drata or equivalent) and turning monitoring into evidence.
  • Proven ability to coordinate audits and customer questionnaires with named control owners.
  • Precise written work; register and Statement of Applicability quality matters.
  • Strong stakeholder management with control owners and auditors.
  • CISA, ISO 27001 Lead Implementer or Auditor, or equivalent professional certification.
